title: Semantic-Aware Subgraph State Space Model for WSI Classification in Histopathology
abstract: Histopathological subtyping relies on the recognition of characteristic histological patterns. These patterns may be expressed by individual tissue structures or by the spatial distribution and co-occurrence of multiple structures, and they often span irregularly shaped tissue regions, termed semantic units in this work. However, conventional patch-based representations may fragment such units and fail to explicitly preserve their internal spatial organization, while efficiently modeling relationships among numerous spatially separated units remains challenging. To address these limitations, we propose the Semantic-Aware Subgraph State Space Model (SASG-SSM), a flexible and efficient framework for whole slide image (WSI) classification. Semantic-Aware Subgraphs (SASGs) first approximate irregularly shaped semantic units by adaptively grouping spatially connected patches guided by class-agnostic visual-semantic priors. By representing patches as graph nodes with adjacency edges, SASGs preserve their internal spatial organization rather than treating them as an unordered set. A Subgraph State Space Module (SG-SSM) subsequently combines a graph neural network encoder for intra-subgraph topology encoding with a Mamba-based state space encoder for efficient contextualization across large numbers of subgraphs. This module integrates local structural information within semantic units with global contextual information arising from their distribution and co-occurrence across the WSI, while efficiently modeling a large number of spatially distributed regions. Extensive experiments across four WSI subtyping datasets demonstrate consistent advantages over representative state-of-the-art methods. Further evaluations under small-cohort and few-shot settings demonstrate robustness and data efficiency under limited training data. Code will be released at https://github.com/HLSvois/SASG-SSM.

title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing: Conceptual Transformation, Strategic Applications, and Future Vision
abstract: Aim: This study aims to investigate the strategic integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into digital marketing, systematically analyzing how cognitive computing redefines traditional and extended marketing paradigms. Methodology: Utilizing a structured conceptual review methodology, this study synthesizes academic literature from core databases (Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar) published between 2010 and 2026. The conceptual framework tracks the evolutionary trajectory of web technologies and maps AI capabilities (Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Natural Language Processing) onto the extended marketing mix (7Ps). Results: The synthesis reveals that AI functions as a key catalyst in transforming the 7Ps from static, standardized organizational functions into dynamic, hyper-personalized, and autonomous value propositions. Sectoral case analyses (such as Netflix, Spotify, FLO, and Nike) demonstrate that the practical application of AI primarily treats experience enrichment, predictive demand forecasting, and operational error reduction. Because this is a conceptual review, quantitative p-values are not applicable; however, the qualitative synthesis establishes a robust linkage between Web 5.0 concepts and emotion-aware marketing strategies. Conclusion: The integration of AI in marketing represents a fundamental shift from intuitive strategies to highly predictable, data-driven frameworks. To sustain competitive advantages, contemporary enterprises must balance technological optimization with strict compliance with data privacy regulations (GDPR/KVKK) and corporate environmental responsibilities regarding the computational carbon footprint of AI models.

title: Reproduction code for: Exact Fock Amplitudes of the Cubic-Phase Gate on Arbitrary Pure Gaussian States
abstract: Reproduction code for the paper "Exact Fock Amplitudes of the Cubic-Phase Gate on Arbitrary Pure Gaussian States" by Ghasem Asadi Cordshooli. A single Python script that regenerates every table and figure in the paper. It implements the closed-form Fock amplitudes of the cubic phase gate acting on an arbitrary pure single-mode Gaussian state, expressed through the Airy function and its derivative, together with an independent high-precision quadrature of the defining integral that the closed form is checked against. It also implements the recurrence in the Fock index, the truncated matrix-exponential construction used as a benchmark, and the consistency checks reported in the text. Requires mpmath, numpy, scipy and matplotlib. Running the script writes the three figure PDFs under the filenames the manuscript expects and prints the three tables, with the reference amplitudes emitted as ready-to-paste LaTeX rows. See README.md for the mapping from each function to the corresponding table, figure or equation of the paper.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Matrix Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic adaptive matrix theory that leverages machine learning to dynamically adjust matrix parameters based on input data. The core mechanism centers around a "Dynamic Matrix Evolution" (DME) process, where the matrix's weights are continuously adjusted to optimize performance in complex systems. We present a novel framework for parameter learning and adaptation, demonstrating its effectiveness in modeling and optimizing various systems. The development of this theory addresses limitations of static matrix representations, providing a more flexible and responsive approach to complex system analysis. This work contributes to the field of dynamic systems modeling and optimization, offering a practical pathway towards automated parameter adjustment within complex environments.

title: 基于量子拓扑的自适应量子电路设计优化
abstract: Quantum circuits, with their inherent complexity and sensitivity to environmental fluctuations, pose significant challenges in their design and implementation. This paper presents a novel framework for quantum circuit design leveraging the principles of quantum topology, specifically a topological circuit design. We propose a self-adaptive circuit design algorithm that automatically adjusts circuit parameters to optimize performance and stability. This approach overcomes limitations of traditional circuit design by exploiting the inherent robustness and adaptability of topological structures. The framework utilizes a set of topological constraints and transformations to dynamically modify the circuit's parameters, leading to improved efficiency and stability. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in optimizing circuit performance across a range of parameters.

title: 基于动态的自适应的深度学习的梯度调整策略
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive gradient adjustment strategy for deep learning models. Traditional gradient adjustment methods often rely on fixed parameters, which can be suboptimal for complex datasets. Our approach leverages data-driven feedback to dynamically adjust the gradient adjustment process, optimizing the model's performance. We propose a framework that continuously monitors the data input and adapts the gradient adjustment strategy accordingly. This adaptation allows the model to effectively navigate complex data landscapes and achieve improved generalization capabilities. The core mechanism is a feedback loop that adjusts the learning rate and/or the gradient adjustment threshold based on the data's variance and the model's error. This adaptive approach significantly enhances the robustness and efficiency of deep learning models. We evaluate the proposed method on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving model accuracy and reducing training time.

title: Title: Bayesian Constraint Optimization with Adaptive Noise Amplification
abstract: Bayesian Constraint Optimization (BCO) is a powerful framework for optimization problems where uncertainty plays a crucial role. However, standard Bayesian inference can be computationally expensive and sensitive to model misspecification. This paper introduces a novel Bayesian approach that dynamically amplifies and refines noise during constraint optimization, leveraging a hierarchical, multi-scale probabilistic model to reduce uncertainty and improve solution robustness. This system employs a "noise amplifier" layer that intelligently prioritizes observations, minimizing the impact of irrelevant data while maximizing the contribution of promising regions of the search space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of benchmark problems, showcasing improved solution quality and robustness compared to existing approaches.

title: Dynamic Constraint-Based Simulation of Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the application of dynamic constraint-based simulation to evolutionary algorithms, aiming to enhance stability and accelerate convergence. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often struggle with convergence issues, particularly when the search space becomes complex and constraints are not properly managed. We propose a novel simulation method that iteratively adjusts constraint sets during the evolutionary process, providing a dynamic mechanism for guiding the algorithm towards a stable and optimal solution. The core of this approach lies in modeling the evolutionary process itself, incorporating constraints that dynamically respond to the algorithm's progress. This dynamic adaptation significantly improves the robustness and efficiency of evolutionary algorithms, offering a potential shift from static constraint application to a more adaptive and potentially faster search strategy.

title: Information-Theoretic Bounds on the Complexity of Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper investigates the inherent complexity of neural network training from an information-theoretic perspective. We establish theoretical bounds on the achievable performance of neural networks by quantifying the information required to represent the training data and the model parameters. These bounds are derived using concepts such as Kolmogorov complexity and mutual information. The primary goal is to provide a rigorous framework for understanding the fundamental limits of training, offering insights that can guide the design of more efficient and effective neural network architectures and training algorithms. We present a novel approach to complexity analysis, shifting the focus from empirical performance metrics to the underlying information requirements, which we demonstrate can provide surprisingly insightful results. The theoretical framework presented here offers a valuable tool for researchers seeking to optimize neural network training and achieve better generalization performance.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement remains a cornerstone of quantum technologies, offering unparalleled capabilities for secure communication and quantum computation. However, the inherent complexity of quantum systems poses significant challenges in terms of modeling, prediction, and control. This paper introduces an adaptive quantum entanglement algorithm designed to address these challenges by dynamically adjusting quantum system parameters, enabling improved model prediction and robustness. We propose a novel approach that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance the representation of complex quantum systems. This algorithm focuses on utilizing the dynamic modification of quantum system states to achieve more accurate and reliable results, effectively mitigating the difficulties associated with quantum entanglement. This work presents a fundamental approach to enhancing the capabilities of quantum systems through intelligent parameter adjustments.

title: Causal Inference on Streaming Data with Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper addresses the critical challenge of performing causal inference on streaming data, a scenario prevalent in modern data environments. Traditional causal inference methods, reliant on static data assumptions, are computationally intractable when applied to continuous streams of information. We propose an algorithm designed for efficient learning and updating of causal relationships within streaming data, leveraging Bayesian Networks and incorporating techniques like online Bayesian model averaging and approximate inference. Our approach aims to provide a practical solution for dynamic causal discovery and inference in environments characterized by constant data flux. The core claim of this work is that applying traditional methods to streaming data is computationally prohibitive. We detail the core mechanism of our algorithm, focusing on its ability to adapt and learn from evolving data patterns. This research contributes to a new paradigm for causal reasoning in dynamic systems, offering a framework for understanding and acting upon the underlying causal drivers of change.

title: Hyper-Adaptive Fuzzy Logic (HFL)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of a hyper-adaptive fuzzy logic system, HFL, to enhance the adaptability of fuzzy logic models to dynamic environments. Traditional fuzzy logic systems often rely on fixed membership functions, limiting their effectiveness in rapidly changing scenarios. The core of this research lies in a novel learning algorithm that continuously refines the fuzzy logic parameters based on real-time data streams, thereby improving the system's responsiveness and robustness. We present a detailed methodology, outlining the key components and implementation details. The benefits of HFL are demonstrated through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing its potential to surpass existing approaches in dynamic system control.

title: Adaptive Neural Symbolic Systems for Embodied AI
abstract: This paper proposes a novel architecture for embodied artificial intelligence (AI) systems, termed Adaptive Neural Symbolic Systems (ANSS). The core challenge in current embodied AI is the reliance on pre-defined, hand-crafted symbolic representations, which hinder adaptability and limit the effectiveness of transfer learning. ANSS addresses this limitation by integrating neural networks with symbolic processing in a dynamically adaptive manner. Specifically, neural networks learn to generate and refine symbolic representations based on sensorimotor experience. A key component, the 'symbolic coherence engine,' provides continuous feedback, evaluating the consistency and utility of these symbols, thereby guiding the neural network's learning process. This creates a closed-loop system where neural and symbolic processing interact, enabling the AI to build a more robust and adaptable internal model of the world. The system is designed to improve performance in environments with varying dynamics and unforeseen circumstances. The architecture leverages the strengths of both neural networks – their ability to learn complex patterns – and symbolic representations – their inherent interpretability and reasoning capabilities – to achieve a synergistic effect. The ultimate goal is to create embodied AI agents that can effectively navigate and interact with complex, real-world environments.

title: 基于图神经网络的复杂事件预测模型
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to complex event prediction utilizing a Graph Neural Network (GNN) architecture. The model is designed to automatically learn and predict the probability of event occurrences, and incorporate anomaly detection capabilities. We explore the application of GNNs to capture intricate relationships within event sequences, leading to more accurate predictions compared to traditional statistical methods. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging GNNs to construct a predictive model that explicitly models event dependencies and propagation. The research emphasizes the model's ability to handle complex scenarios and its potential for enhanced anomaly detection.

title: 自适应的深度学习的自然语言处理的文本生成模型优化
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of text generation models using an adaptive deep learning approach. Traditional methods often employ fixed parameters, limiting the model's ability to handle complex text structures. This research proposes a novel method that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on textual characteristics, resulting in improved text quality and diversity, and ultimately, more effective text generation. The core mechanism centers around an adaptive learning algorithm that continuously refines the model's parameters to better suit the input text. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through empirical evaluation on several benchmark datasets. The resulting model exhibits superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

title: Quantum Network Key Distribution Protocol Topological Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of topological structures within quantum key distribution (QKD) protocols. The core claim is that strategic topological optimization can significantly enhance key distribution efficiency and security. The proposed methodology leverages analytical analysis of quantum network topologies to identify optimal key distribution schemes. Specifically, we explore how the arrangement of nodes and connections within a quantum network impacts the performance of protocols like BB84 and E91. The underlying mechanism involves utilizing the inherent properties of quantum entanglement to achieve highly efficient and secure key exchange. We present a framework for evaluating different topological configurations based on metrics such as key generation rate, channel loss, and eavesdropping detection probability. The results demonstrate a clear correlation between optimized topologies and improved QKD performance. Furthermore, we address the challenges associated with implementing these optimized topologies, including considerations for quantum repeater placement and network scalability. This research contributes to the advancement of practical QKD systems by providing a rigorous approach to topological design.

title: Algorithmic Transparency via Formal Verification of Code-Generated Explanations
abstract: The increasing reliance on AI systems across various domains raises critical concerns about algorithmic transparency and trust. Many AI explanations, particularly those generated by code, are inherently opaque, making it challenging for humans to understand, verify, and ultimately trust the reasoning behind these systems' decisions. This paper proposes a novel framework for achieving algorithmic transparency through the formal verification of code-generated explanations. Our approach focuses on rigorously analyzing these explanations for logical consistency, factual accuracy, and adherence to predefined constraints. We introduce a formal verification process that leverages mathematical logic and automated reasoning to provide a robust guarantee of explanation trustworthiness. The core claim of this work is that explanations generated by AI are often opaque and difficult to verify, and our framework offers a practical solution to address this challenge. This research contributes significantly to the field of explainable AI (XAI) by establishing a methodology for systematically assessing and validating AI explanations, fostering greater accountability and user confidence in AI-driven systems. ---

title: Title: Bayesian Network for Complex Network Analysis
abstract: Complex network structures exhibit intricate dependencies and inherent uncertainty, posing significant challenges for traditional network analysis. This paper introduces a Bayesian Network (BN) approach to address this challenge, providing a robust framework for quantifying network behavior based on probabilistic inference. We formulate a BN that explicitly represents dependencies and uncertainty, enabling more accurate and reliable analysis compared to approximation-based methods. The core mechanism involves Bayesian inference to determine the probability of different network states, incorporating uncertainty directly into the model. This leads to a more principled and versatile approach for understanding and modeling complex network dynamics.

evidence.title: Title: Bayesian Network for Complex Network Analysis
evidence.abstract: Complex network structures exhibit intricate dependencies and inherent uncertainty, posing significant challenges for traditional network analysis. This paper introduces a Bayesian Network (BN) approach to address this challenge, providing a robust framework for quantifying network behavior based on probabilistic inference. We formulate a BN that explicitly represents dependencies and uncertainty, enabling more accurate and reliable analysis compared to approximation-based methods. The core mechanism involves Bayesian inference to determine the probability of different network states, incorporating uncertainty directly into the model. This leads to a more principled and versatile approach for understanding and modeling complex network dynamics.

title: Bayesian Constraint Optimization for Quantum State Design
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian constraint optimization framework for quantum state design, aiming to accelerate the discovery of optimal quantum states through iterative refinement of parameters. The framework leverages a probabilistic model that weighs potential states based on observed entanglement and decoherence, utilizing a dynamically updated prior derived from repeated simulations. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional heuristics by incorporating a robust, probabilistic analysis, promising significant improvements in the efficiency of quantum state design. The core mechanism involves a Bayesian model that continuously updates the prior based on simulation results, guiding the search towards more promising states. The paper details the model architecture, the rationale behind the probabilistic weighting, and the simulation methodology used to demonstrate the framework's effectiveness. The results showcase a substantial reduction in the search space compared to conventional methods, highlighting the potential for significantly faster and more accurate quantum state design.

title: Quantum Adaptive Adaptation of Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum adaptive learning framework leveraging the inherent self-adaptative properties of quantum states. Traditional machine learning methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their effectiveness, particularly in scenarios with sparse data. We propose a quantum-enhanced learning paradigm that dynamically adjusts key parameters based on quantum state fluctuations, enabling more efficient learning and improved performance in data-scarce environments. The core mechanism involves manipulating the quantum state to induce a feedback loop that optimizes the learning process. This approach offers a fundamentally different approach to parameter optimization, potentially surpassing the limitations of conventional techniques. The paper details the theoretical framework, implementation of the quantum adaptation algorithm, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its efficacy.

title: Graph-based Machine Learning Dynamic Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning model, Graph-based Machine Learning Dynamic Adjustment, that automatically adjusts model parameters to adapt to evolving data. The core idea revolves around representing data as a graph, enabling the model to dynamically adjust its parameters based on graph structure changes. Traditional machine learning methods often require manual parameter tuning, which is a computationally expensive and time-consuming process. This approach offers an automated and efficient mechanism for model adaptation, leading to improved generalization performance. The paper details the design of the model, its underlying principles, and the potential benefits of its implementation.

title: Adaptive Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is a revolutionary cryptographic protocol that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to secure communication. Traditional methods rely on computationally weak algorithms, making them vulnerable to eavesdropping. QKD offers unparalleled security based on the fundamental laws of physics, ensuring that any attempt to intercept the key will be immediately detectable. This paper explores the development of an adaptive quantum key distribution (AQKD) protocol, designed to dynamically adjust to environmental noise, thereby enhancing key security and reliability. We detail the core mechanism, highlighting how the protocol leverages quantum entanglement to create a resilient key distribution system. Our analysis focuses on improving the robustness against noise and ensuring consistent security throughout the key generation process.

title: Data and code for: Can human experts verify machine-learning detected earthquakes?
abstract: Data and code accompanying the manuscript Can human experts verify machine-learning detected earthquakes? Six machine-learning earthquake catalogues were audited with a stratified blind expert panel. Four seismologists returned 4,800 waveform-level verdicts on 1,200 events across six sequences (Ridgecrest, Iquique, Amatrice, NE Japan forearc, ToC2ME and Kīlauea), judging metadata-stripped record sections as confirmed, unresolved or rejected. This archive contains: de-identified verdict tables (reviewers labelled R1-R4, ordered by fitted leniency); the stratified panel designs and sampling weights; waveform feature tables; confirmability-scored catalogues for all six sequences; the correlation-dimension and double-seismic-zone results; every analysis and figure script; and the typeset manuscript with its supplementary information. Reviewer names are given only in Table S5 of the manuscript and are not present in the data files. Funding. U.S. National Science Foundation award EAR-2506181.

title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Financial Frauds Detection: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Financial frauds are rising and becoming very common in this modern technology-driven era. Specifically, financial frauds are the type of fraud that can be committed by just sitting at a remote location and clicking some buttons on a laptop or by setting an algorithm. Hence, the detection and prevention of financial fraud becomes a big challenge for the banking industry. In order to detect and deal with these frauds, artificial intelligence is playing an important role by providing advanced technologies such as machine learning. The present study attempts to map the knowledge structure in the domain of artificial intelligence and its application for financial fraud detection. For this purpose, the data is obtained from a widely used Scopus database, and bibliometric analysis is applied using VOSviewer Software. The present study analysed 63 articles published from 2015 to October 2024. The findings of the study reveal that after 2019, sharp growth has been seen in studies related to exploring the role of artificial intelligence in detecting financial fraud. The continent of Asia majorly contributed to the literature in the domain of applying artificial intelligence in detecting financial frauds followed by the continents of Europe and America.

title: From FastText to GPT-4o and DeepSeek: Architecture-Aware Benchmarking for Multimodal and Scientific Reasoning
abstract: There has been a great revolution in Natural Language Processing (NLP) since Large Language Models (LLMs). These models work to help machines better understand and respond to human language. Machine translation, chatbots, content generation, and even healthcare diagnostics have advanced thanks to models like Generative pretrained transformer (GPT) and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), which leverage transformer architecture. Today, they are a must-have in virtually every industry as a means to increase automation, customer engagement and use data more intelligently. LLMs simplify workflows and increase productivity in software development, helping with code writing and debugging. They also see frequent use in sentiment analysis and recommendation systems that allow companies to take better decisions. The announcement of OpenAI&s;s GPT-1 in 2018 represented an important, new advancement in the evolution of LLMs. InstructGPT arrived in 2022 with an improved interaction quality thanks to Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). OpenAI, which coined the term “GPT-4o”, recently released the (larger and faster) GPT-4o in 2024). Focusing especially on its precision and efficacy of results, DeepSeek has ranked among the best in LLM. This article compares ChatGPT and DeepSeek to analyze what roles they have in the current AI ecosystem regarding performance, architecture principles, and applications.

title: MedProb: Probing Internal Representations of Vision-Language Models for Medical Question Answering
abstract: Medical visual question answering (Med-VQA) is often assumed to require medical fine-tuning, large models, or complex multi-agent pipelines. We revisit this assumption with \textbf{MedProb}, a lightweight probing framework that predicts multiple-choice Med-VQA answers from frozen VLM representations without free-text generation. Across PATH-VQA, SLAKE, and VQA-RAD, MedProb recovers substantially more answer-relevant signal than prompting and performs stronger than medical VLMs and agentic systems. Probing also reduces the apparent gap between small and large models compared to prompting, suggesting that smaller VLMs contain more recoverable Med-VQA signal than generation-based evaluation reveals. Across 14 matched general-purpose and medical VLM pairs, medical adaptation does not consistently improve this linear decodability. Finally, free-text generation exhibits an answer-position bias of up to 10 percentage points, whereas MedProb also has positional bias, however, it is impacted differently than prompting. Our main results target the multiple-choice/multiclass Med-VQA setting; we additionally show the probe can be extended to open-ended generation via a rejection-sampling scoring procedure.

title: Fixed Suffix Dependency Ratio: Quantifying the Dual-Track Mechanism of Gender Assignment in Latvian Loanwords
abstract: Existing research has repeatedly observed the tendency for English loanwords to cluster in the masculine gender across different recipient languages, yet the origin of this pattern remains difficult to determine, as fixed morphological rules and default assignments are frequently analysed together. This study proposes the Fixed Suffix Dependency Ratio (FSDR) to quantify the degree of reliance on fixed derivational suffixes across different genders, and to distinguish between morphological anchoring and free-choice in distribution. By examining 1,832 Latvian noun lemma types, the results reveal a significant FSDR asymmetry within the loanword system: feminine loanwords rely significantly more on fixed derivational suffixes, while masculine loanwords are more concentrated in the free-choice zone. This pattern exhibits loanword specificity and has become more pronounced in contemporary usage. FSDR therefore provides a quantitative framework for testing default gender and shows how masculine default can be activated and reinforced under language contact.

title: Binned semiparametric Bayesian networks for efficient kernel density estimation
abstract: This paper introduces a new type of probabilistic semiparametric model that takes advantage of data binning to reduce the computational cost of kernel density estimation in nonparametric distributions. Two new conditional probability distributions are developed for the new binned semiparametric Bayesian networks: the sparse binned kernel density estimation and the Fourier kernel density estimation. These two probability distributions address the curse of dimensionality, which typically impacts binned models, by using sparse tensors and restricting the number of parent nodes in conditional probability calculations. To evaluate the proposal, we perform a complexity analysis and conduct several comparative experiments using synthetic data and datasets from the UCI Machine Learning repository. The experiments include different binning rules, parent restrictions, grid sizes, and sample sizes to obtain a holistic view of the model’s behavior. As a result, our binned semiparametric Bayesian networks achieve structural learning and log-likelihood estimations with no statistically significant differences compared to standard semiparametric Bayesian networks, but at significantly higher speeds. Thus, the new binned semiparametric Bayesian networks prove to be a reliable and more efficient alternative to their non-binned counterparts.

title: Instruction Duplication as an Inference-Time Control Primitive
abstract: Procedural instruction following is a basic requirement for controllable language-model systems, especially when generated trajectories are inspected or repaired downstream. We introduce instruction duplication, a minimal black-box inference-time control that repeats only the procedural instruction, without retraining or decoding changes. Across seven instruction-tuned models, 300 medical multiple-choice questions, eight placement conditions, and 16,800 scheduled generations, moving from one to two copies raises the deterministic All-8 diagnostic--responses passing all eight observable tests--from 90.22% to 93.17% (+2.95 percentage points), eliminating 30.2% of the failures remaining after one copy. Pre-provisional TF-IDF recall rises from 73.44% to 74.81% (+1.38 points; Holm-adjusted p < .001), while final-answer accuracy remains exactly 60.21%. Premature commitment increases from 1.52% to 2.30% (p_Holm = .00536). A blinded challenge audit yields 10/30 directional confirmations, 20/30 perceptual ties, and no reversals; its prespecified 28/30 confirmation criterion is not met. Yet this distinction can matter operationally when a downstream system acts on the generated trajectory. In Answer Engineering (AE), where explicit trajectory state determines local repair, the published reason-first no-editing SSNHL endpoint was 25.1%; system-only AE was later reproduced at 84.2%, and the same trailing duplicate raised it to 97.1%. For conductive diagnostic branch preservation, the corresponding values are 58.9% published without editing, 78.6% with reproduced AE, and 73.8% with AE plus duplication--a within-AE decrease, but still 14.9 points above the no-editing baseline. Instruction duplication is therefore a low-complexity, placement-sensitive control whose practical value can emerge through the downstream system that consumes the exposed trajectory.

title: What Moves? Localized Motion Representations for Compositional Scene Control
abstract: Real-world dynamics are inherently compositional: multiple entities move simultaneously within a shared scene, each exhibiting distinct motion patterns. Yet current motion representation models entangle the dynamics of different entities, without explicitly capturing localized motion for each individually. Crucially, motion is defined relative to a global reference frame, including camera motion and scene layout. However, localized embeddings are often computed from cropped images or obtained by masking features after encoding, discarding the context needed to interpret motion. To address this, we introduce a promptable localized motion representation that produces persistent embeddings for user-specified regions defined by spatial masks. Rather than cropping the input or masking features, our model processes the full video and conditions motion encoding directly on the queried region. This yields temporally consistent, region-addressable embeddings that isolate local dynamics while retaining the global context required for disambiguation. We demonstrate object-level motion transfer, enabling controlled composition of dynamic scenes. Beyond generative control, our embeddings support localized action classification in multi-actor videos. Across both tasks, our approach improves controllability and outperforms global representations localized through cropping or post-hoc masking.

title: A Circuit for Plural Reference: How LLMs Represent and Retrieve Singular and Plural Entities
abstract: Coreference resolution is an important task in contextual reasoning. In this paper, we investigate the mechanism for representing and retrieving singular and plural entities for plural reference. We use a combination of mechanistic interpretability and attention pattern analysis to study the process in which LLMs predict a pronoun to refer back to previously mentioned entities. Using a range of causal intervention techniques, we find a set of attention heads that are responsible for (1) representing coreference information in the input, (2) identifying entities that form a plural reference, (3) transferring the information to the component that is responsible for selecting the antecedents and predicting the pronoun. We also find that LLMs align with humans in preference for plural pronoun. Specifically, entities in a plural construction are more likely to be referred to as a plural entity if they are ontologically similar and are linked by the conjunction "and".

title: Counterfactual Routing Using Integer Programming with Constraint Generation
abstract: We present our submission to the IJCAI 2025 'Counterfactual Routing Competition' (CRC 25). The goal of the competition is to find counterfactual explanations for the shortest path problem. This requires deciding what the minimal changes to a road network would make a route chosen by the user the optimal route. This enables explanations such as "Your suggested route would indeed have been optimal, if road X were not a bicycle path." Our solution models the problem as an integer program, iteratively incorporating constraints until an exact solution is found. In the final evaluation on held-out test instances, our method ranked fourth in solution quality and obtained its solution fastest on every instance, with an average runtime of 9.0 seconds compared to 118.8 seconds for the next-fastest submission.

This enables explanations such as "Your suggested route would indeed have been optimal, if road X were not a bicycle path." Our solution models the problem as an integer program, iteratively incorporating constraints until an exact solution is found. In the final evaluation on held-out test instances, our method ranked fourth in solution quality and obtained its solution fastest on every instance, with an average runtime of 9.0 seconds compared to 118.8 seconds for the next-fastest submission.

title: Preprocessing Failure and Adversarial Detection in Depthwise-Separable Edge Vision Systems
abstract: Preprocessing-based defenses are the standard first-line response to adversarial attacks on edge vision systems, requiring no retraining, no architectural changes, and widely recommended as model-agnostic mitigations. Yet the foundational evaluations of these defenses were conducted on residual or Inception-class architectures, not on the depthwise-separable CNNs that dominate edge deployments. This untested assumption leaves a gap in the security evaluation literature. This paper closes that gap by evaluating six preprocessing defenses against adversarial perturbations across both architecture families. Across all perturbation levels and defenses tested, the two depthwise-separable architectures show consistently poor recovery while the residual architecture shows partial recovery; ablation results are consistent with an architectural rather than parametric explanation, though only three architectures and one attack family are evaluated. Crucially, this failure is not merely a negative result. The same output divergence that disqualifies preprocessing as a recovery mechanism reveals a detection opportunity: preprocessing consistently disrupts clean predictions while leaving adversarial predictions largely unchanged, an asymmetry that is directly measurable without retraining or architectural modification. We further show that standard image quality metrics are unreliable proxies for defense effectiveness, a methodological gap in current evaluation practice. A practitioner decision framework is provided for adversarially resilient edge vision deployment.

title: Internship Placement Recommendation for Final Year Students Using a Fuzzy Logic System of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: This study presents a Fuzzy Logic System (FLS) to support final-year Bachelor of Science (Hons.) Mathematics students at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), Shah Alam in selecting suitable internship placements. The project aims to identify key decision-making criteria, develop a fuzzy logic control system, and evaluate its effectiveness and usability. Unlike traditional methods, the system handles uncertainty and subjective preferences through fuzzy logic. Based on literature review and student interviews, four main criteria were selected: salary, location, job opportunity, and organizational reputation. Using the Mamdani inference method in MATLAB, the model was designed with triangular membership functions and a rule base. To test the system, data from three final-year students were analyzed, comparing their actual internship choices with system recommendations. Results showed that the system produced appropriate and reliable suggestions, while usability testing confirmed that the interface was simple and helpful for decision-making. Overall, the project successfully met all objectives, demonstrating the value of fuzzy logic in addressing the complexity of internship selection. Future improvements may include adding more criteria and developing a web or mobile platform to increase accessibility and impact.

title: Inteligencia artificial en nuevos emprendimientos: revisión crítica del desempeño empresarial
abstract: La presente revisión tuvo como objetivo analizar la relación entre adoptar herramientas de IA y el desempeño empresarial de los nuevos emprendimientos, a fin de proponer lineamientos estratégicos. Se revisó críticamente la literatura publicada entre 2021 y 2026 con un enfoque cualitativo de tipo documental, se registró cada publicación en una matriz de análisis documental y la información fue procesada mediante análisis de contenido temático organizado en cuatro categorías. La revisión identificó cinco herramientas con eficacia documentada, la IA generativa, el aprendizaje automático, la analítica predictiva, los sistemas de inteligencia de negocios y los chatbots inteligentes, y mostró que sus beneficios sobre la productividad, la eficiencia operativa, la innovación y la competitividad dependen menos de la herramienta que de la organización que la adopta. Formar digitalmente al equipo, liderar el cambio, cuidar la calidad de los datos y alinear la tecnología con la estrategia explican por qué emprendimientos con recursos similares obtienen resultados distintos. Con estos hallazgos el estudio construyó el Modelo Estratégico para la Adopción de Inteligencia Artificial en Nuevos Emprendimientos (MEAINE), que ordena la incorporación de estas tecnologías en cinco componentes, del diagnóstico organizacional a la evaluación continua, y concluye que la IA fortalece al emprendimiento en la medida en que este desarrolla la capacidad de aprovecharla.

title: The Graph Is the Memory: An Architecture for Learned Routing, Crystallizing Knowledge, and Measured Growth over a Fleet of Language Models
abstract: We present an architecture in which routing and memory are the same structure. Tasks project onto facets; facets connect to actions (models, adapters, templates, extracted composites) through weighted edges; the edge graph is simultaneously the routing policy and the system's memory of which work belongs where. Reading memory is summing edges, writing memory is a forward-only delta rule, and because the representation is strictly additive, recall generalizes to facet combinations never seen. Knowledge crystallizes into progressively cheaper forms (edge weights, an exact-match cache, admission-gated composite actions, low-rank adapters distilled from the system's own accepted solves, and tiered shared stores), so the system becomes faster and cheaper as it runs. Results, each pre-registered and scored by a mechanical oracle rather than a judge model: a learned router matched a frontier-only control on accept rate at roughly 31 percent lower cost per accepted solve; a specialist adapter trained on the system's own record raised held-out accepts on its cell from 48.0 to 90.7 percent; a from-scratch discovery organ proposed a task partition no human named, which was admitted by evidence, wired into the live router, and whose first gated activation recovered reward at 35.7 and 4.0 standard errors; and concurrent learners consolidated with zero lost updates. We also report a load-bearing negative result: under the corrected reward currency, every composite previously admitted by an accept-only condition was reward-negative, and the growth layer's remaining claim is stated as an open, pre-registered program. Every claim in the report is labeled proven, partial, or open, and every number traces to a run artifact. This is version 0.2 of an ongoing research program; later versions will fold in registered experiments as they resolve.

title: 基于自适应量子拓扑的量子电路优化
abstract: This paper explores the application of self-adaptive quantum topology for optimizing quantum circuits. Traditional quantum circuit optimization methods often rely on classical algorithms, whereas this research introduces a novel approach leveraging the unique properties of quantum topology to enhance circuit efficiency and performance. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts the topology of quantum circuits, resulting in improved performance metrics. The core of this approach involves a sophisticated algorithm that analyzes and modifies the quantum circuit's topology based on a learned model, optimizing for specific performance criteria. The significance of this work lies in its potential to significantly improve the efficiency and scalability of quantum computations through a fundamentally different optimization paradigm. We present a conceptual framework, demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach through simplified examples and highlighting the potential for broader applicability.

title: Quantum-Inspired Data Structures for Parallel Processing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum-inspired data structures to revolutionize parallel processing, specifically focusing on design principles that mimic the phenomena of quantum entanglement. The core claim is that by leveraging data structures that inherently exploit these principles, we can significantly enhance the efficiency of parallel computations, particularly for large datasets. We investigate several promising data structure types – quantum walks and entanglement graphs – and analyze their potential to optimize data access and communication in parallel environments. The paper details the theoretical underpinnings of these structures, proposes an optimization strategy, and discusses the challenges and future research directions for this emerging field.

title: Hyper-Dimensionality Clustering (HDC)
abstract: This paper introduces Hyper-Dimensionality Clustering (HDC), a novel algorithm designed to identify clusters of data points within high-dimensional spaces. Traditional clustering methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of these datasets, failing to effectively capture nuanced patterns. HDC addresses this challenge by introducing a novel approach centered on the concept of "density" – a measure quantifying the interconnectedness and distribution of data points across multiple dimensions. The proposed algorithm dynamically adjusts cluster boundaries based on this density, enhancing the discovery of hidden correlations and allowing for the identification of subtle, complex patterns that traditional methods miss. This research explores the potential of HDC to unlock valuable insights from high-dimensional data across various domains, including image analysis, sensor data, and genomic data.

title: Adaptive Quantum Circuit Design & Topology Mapping
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum circuit design utilizing adaptive parameter adjustment. Traditional circuit design methods are often constrained by fixed parameters, limiting the potential for efficient and flexible quantum computations. We introduce a dynamic adjustment mechanism that allows for real-time adjustments to quantum circuit parameters, enabling a significantly enhanced level of control and optimization. The core principle behind this method lies in leveraging quantum phenomena, specifically entanglement and superposition, to dynamically modify the circuit's evolution, leading to improved performance and novel functionalities. The resulting design offers a pathway to overcome limitations inherent in fixed-parameter approaches, opening doors to more complex and sophisticated quantum algorithms. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this adaptive strategy through simulations and analysis, showcasing its potential to revolutionize quantum circuit design.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Geometric Simulation of Complex Flows
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-enhanced geometric simulation to complex fluid flows, aiming to significantly improve accuracy and speed compared to traditional numerical methods. The core claim is to develop a novel quantum-based technique that utilizes quantum algorithms to represent fluid states and dynamics, leading to enhanced computational efficiency and precision. We explore the potential of leveraging quantum phenomena such as superposition and entanglement to address the inherent challenges of simulating fluid behavior, particularly those involving complex geometries and rapid changes. The paper presents a conceptual framework, outlines the key algorithmic steps, and discusses the challenges and opportunities inherent in this research area. The study emphasizes the transformative potential of quantum computing for fluid dynamics, paving the way for more accurate and efficient simulations of intricate flow phenomena.

title: Title: Information-Theoretic Geometry – Self-Organizing Data Structures
abstract: This paper explores the application of information theory to the design of novel data structures with inherent self-organization and fractal characteristics. Traditional data structure approaches often rely on predefined algorithms and rigid structures. We propose a framework that leverages information-theoretic measures, specifically entropy and Kolmogorov complexity, to guide the generation of data structures that exhibit self-similarity and adaptive complexity. The core mechanism involves embedding the data structure within a probabilistic space, where the structure's properties are determined by the interplay of information and the underlying probability distribution. This approach aims to overcome limitations of existing data structures by promoting a dynamic, self-organizing behavior. The paper details the mathematical foundations of this framework, discusses the initial implementation of a prototype data structure, and presents preliminary results demonstrating the emergence of self-similarity and efficient processing characteristics. The investigation highlights the potential for a paradigm shift in data structure design, moving beyond fixed algorithms towards a more adaptive and self-organizing approach.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Neural Network Parameter Adjustment Strategy
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive neural network parameter adjustment strategy designed to effectively model and identify complex data distributions. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the model's ability to adapt to varying data characteristics. Our proposed approach dynamically adjusts network parameters based on observed data features, allowing the model to learn and generalize better. This results in improved performance across diverse datasets, particularly in scenarios with significant data variability. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that iteratively refines the parameter adjustments based on the model's output, ensuring optimal performance. This work presents a robust and adaptable framework for parameter optimization within neural network architectures.

title: Adaptive Feature Priming via Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to machine learning – Adaptive Feature Priming via Evolutionary Algorithms – that aims to automatically discover optimal feature combinations for improved model performance. Traditional feature engineering relies heavily on human expertise, which can be time-consuming and may not always yield the best results. Our method leverages the power of evolutionary algorithms, specifically genetic algorithms, to dynamically adaptively prime features. The core idea is to evolve a population of feature combinations, evaluating each combination's effectiveness on a specific target task. The algorithm iteratively refines these combinations, selecting the most promising ones to 'prime' the features before applying them to the learning process. This approach represents a shift from manual feature engineering to an automated, adaptive strategy, potentially leading to significant performance gains and reduced reliance on domain expertise. The method is presented with a comprehensive theoretical framework and the core mechanisms are detailed.

title: Title: Information-Theoretic Constraints for Neural Network Architecture Optimization
abstract: The design of neural network architectures is a complex process, often relying on trial-and-error to discover optimal configurations. This paper proposes a novel framework for neural network architecture optimization leveraging information-theoretic constraints. We introduce a method that guides the network's structure through the application of entropy measures, promoting efficient learning and generalization by encouraging solutions that maximize information gain. The core mechanism involves constructing a network structure with explicitly defined constraints derived from information theory, which are then iteratively refined via an optimization process. This approach aims to overcome limitations of traditional methods by introducing a principled approach to architecture design, potentially resulting in more robust and efficient models. This work directly addresses the challenge of designing architectures that are both accurate and easily generalizeable.

title: Quantum Topologies: Adaptive Geometry Optimization for Quantum Computing Efficiency
abstract: Quantum Topologies, a novel approach to quantum computing, leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum states to achieve computational advantages. This paper investigates the potential of dynamically evolving quantum states to optimize quantum computation, addressing the inherent computational complexity associated with traditional methods. We propose a novel algorithm, termed "Dynamic Topology Optimization," which utilizes a transient, adaptive geometry to reduce computational complexity and enhance efficiency. The core mechanism centers around the instantaneous transformation of quantum states, enabling a more intelligent and streamlined quantum processing pipeline. This research explores the benefits of dynamic geometry in enhancing the performance of quantum algorithms.

title: Neural Feedback Optimization Algorithm (NFOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Neural Feedback Optimization Algorithm (NFOA), a novel approach to complex computation that leverages the principles of synaptic plasticity within biological neural networks and combines them with reinforcement learning. NFOA constructs a virtual neural network where computational units, termed "neurons," are interconnected via channels representing data flow. Crucially, each connection exhibits plasticity, with its weight adjusted based on the output of the connected neuron and a defined reward signal. The algorithm utilizes a reinforcement learning framework, specifically Proximal Policy Optimization, to train these connections, striving to maximize the reward and thus optimize the computational process. A key innovation lies in the inclusion of a feedback mechanism allowing neurons to dynamically adjust the sensitivity of connections based on their own activation state, mirroring the dynamic synaptic plasticity observed in biological neural networks. This approach offers a potential pathway to overcome the performance limitations of traditional reinforcement learning methods in complex computational tasks by incorporating a more biologically plausible and adaptive system. The core claim is that by simulating synaptic plasticity and integrating reinforcement learning, NFOA achieves adaptive and optimized solutions for complex calculations.

title: 基于自适应的深度学习的正则化方法
abstract: This paper proposes a novel adaptive regularization method for deep learning models. Traditional regularization techniques often rely on fixed parameter values, limiting their effectiveness in handling data variability. This work introduces a dynamic adjustment of regularization parameters, allowing the model to automatically adapt to the data landscape and improve generalization. The method utilizes a self-adaptive strategy to optimize model performance through iterative refinement of the regularization strength. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously assesses the model's performance on validation data, adjusting the regularization parameters to minimize the loss function. This adaptive approach offers a promising avenue for enhancing deep learning model robustness and accuracy.

title: Algorithmic Uncertainty Quantification via Meta-Learning
abstract: Algorithmic uncertainty quantification (AUQ) is a critical component for building robust and reliable artificial intelligence systems. Current methods often struggle to provide meaningful uncertainty estimates, particularly when applied to complex algorithms or evolving data distributions. This work introduces a novel meta-learning framework designed to address this challenge. The framework learns to predict the uncertainty associated with the output of a given algorithm, trained on a distribution of input data. Unlike traditional error estimation techniques, this approach generates calibrated confidence measures, reflecting the true uncertainty inherent in the algorithm's predictions. The core of the method lies in training a meta-learner to predict the variance or entropy of the algorithm's output distribution, given a set of inputs. This allows for a principled quantification of uncertainty, facilitating informed decision-making and risk mitigation in AI applications. The framework's ability to adapt and learn from diverse datasets makes it particularly well-suited for real-world scenarios where data distributions are constantly shifting. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach through theoretical analysis and outline key design considerations for practical implementation.

title: Hierarchical State Space Reconstruction for Robotic Perception
abstract: This paper presents a novel hierarchical state space reconstruction method designed to overcome the limitations of traditional approaches in high-dimensional robotic environments. The core concept revolves around decomposing the state space into a hierarchy of clusters using a self-organizing map (SOM). This hierarchical representation significantly reduces the complexity of perception and control, enabling more efficient and robust robot operation. The method maps robot actions to these hierarchical levels, creating a multi-level control scheme. The key innovation lies in the structured decomposition, providing a scalable solution to the challenges inherent in traditional state space reconstruction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework, outlining the principles and potential benefits of this method. The presented framework offers a promising direction for enhancing robotic perception and control in complex, dynamic environments.

title: Module-Adaptive General Algorithm Framework
abstract: This paper presents a novel module-adaptive general algorithm framework designed to achieve scalability and adaptability in algorithm construction and configuration. The core innovation lies in the decomposition of algorithm design into modular components, employing self-adaptive adjustment mechanisms to optimize interactions between these modules. We explore a method for dynamically adjusting module parameters and connections to enhance the algorithm's robustness and responsiveness to varying input conditions. The framework's primary goal is to facilitate the creation of highly flexible and extensible algorithms suitable for a wide range of applications. This work introduces a design paradigm that emphasizes modularity and self-optimization, offering a significant advancement in algorithm design and implementation. The presented methodology provides a foundation for constructing adaptable systems with improved performance and ease of modification.

title: Quantum Information Multi-Body Simulation for Quantum Entanglement Computation
abstract: Quantum information theory has opened up unprecedented possibilities for computation, particularly in the realm of quantum entanglement. However, harnessing entanglement requires sophisticated computational techniques, and existing simulation methods often struggle to accurately capture the complex dynamics of multi-body quantum systems. This research presents a novel quantum information multi-body simulation framework that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve significantly improved accuracy and efficiency in the modeling of quantum entanglement evolution. The core mechanism involves constructing a simulation framework where entanglement acts as a fundamental resource, facilitating the precise representation and analysis of entangled states. This approach overcomes limitations of traditional methods by offering a more robust and nuanced understanding of quantum phenomena, ultimately paving the way for enhanced quantum computing capabilities.

title: Self-Adaptive Graph Neural Network Dynamic Graph Structure Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive graph neural network (GNN) dynamic graph structure optimization method. Traditional GNN architectures often rely on static graph representations, limiting their ability to adapt to complex data and improve generalization. We propose a new approach that dynamically adjusts the graph structure during training using an adaptive algorithm. This adaptation allows the model to learn optimal graph representations and parameters, leading to enhanced model performance. The core mechanism involves iteratively refining the graph structure based on the training process, resulting in a more robust and efficient model. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets. The resulting model exhibits superior performance across multiple metrics, highlighting the benefits of dynamic graph structure optimization.

title: Towards a New Computational Paradigm
abstract: This chapter traces the emergence of a new computational paradigm shaped by advances in neural networks, generative models, and multimodal intelligence. It outlines the evolution from expert systems – rule-based and deterministic – to adaptive learning systems capable of inference and creativity. The rise of architectures such as transformers and large language models redefines computation from retrieval to generation, enabling machines to reason across textual, visual, and spatial modalities. In this framework, computation evolves from a closed process of execution to an open, generative ecology capable of modelling, simulating, and reasoning about the world. The chapter situates this shift as both technological and epistemological, redefining how creativity, problem-solving, and design knowledge are constructed in the age of intelligent computation.

title: Generative AI as the second wave of cognitive externalization
abstract: Purpose : to clarify the theoretical and methodological grounds for interpreting generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) as the second wave of cognitive externalization and to reveal the organizational and economic and marketing consequences of this process. Methods : the study is designed as a systematized conceptual and integrative review and uses PRISMA logic to ensure transparency of the source search, cleaning and selection. Two bodies of literature – on writing and on GenAI – are compared in international article databases; an additional full-text control search was conducted in the Russian Science Citation Index. The sources were analyzed taking into account their theoretical density, cognitive function and suitability for economic and marketing interpretation. Results : cognitive offloading is shown as a mechanism for reducing the load on memory, attention and primary information processing, whereas cognitive externalization describes a broader transfer of cognitive functions into external symbolic, material and computational systems. Writing established external memory and repeated access to meaning; GenAI becomes involved in intermediate operations of knowledge work: task framing, criteria formation, generation of alternatives, argumentation and preparation of a preliminary decision framework. Thus, not only the speed of text production changes, but also the distribution of responsibility for task framing, result verification and choice. Conclusions and Relevance : the article proposes an interpretive framework that allows considering GenAI as external procedural mediation. For marketing, this means changes in professional competences, work with market information, choice interfaces and value formation mechanisms. The practical implications require further empirical testing in organizations, marketing departments and sectoral markets.

title: Deceptive bias measurement in deep learning: Assessing shortcut reliance in TCGA cancer models
abstract: Abstract Bias in machine learning is a persistent challenge because it can create unfair outcomes, limit generalization, and reduce trust in real-world applications. A key source of this problem is shortcut learning, where models exploit signals linked to sensitive attributes, such as data source or collection site, instead of relying on task, relevant features. To tackle this, we propose the Deceptive Signal metric, a novel quantitative measure designed to assess the extent of a model’s reliance on hidden shortcuts during the learning process. This metric is derived via the Deceptive Bias Detection pipeline, which isolates shortcut dependence by contrasting model behavior under two controlled conditions: (1) Full Exclusion, where a sensitive subgroup is completely removed from training; and (2) Partial Exclusion, where the model has limited access to specific classes within the subgroup. By calculating the behavioral shift between these settings, the Deceptive Signal metric provides a concrete value representing the model’s proneness to learning task-irrelevant patterns. In experiments with the TCGA histopathology dataset, our metric successfully quantified strong dependencies on center-specific artifacts in models trained for cancer classification. Author summary Deep learning models are becoming powerful tools in healthcare, but they often suffer from a critical vulnerability: they can get the right answer for the wrong reason. In medical imaging, an AI might correctly identify a tumor not by analyzing the tissue, but by recognizing irrelevant digital markers unique to the specific hospital or scanner that produced the image. This phenomenon, known as shortcut learning, makes AI systems appear accurate at first glance while remaining unreliable for real-world patient care. To solve this, our research moves beyond simple accuracy checks and introduces a specific quantitative metric for shortcut learning. We developed a testing framework that forces the model into controlled training scenarios, deliberately withholding specific “shortcut” information to see how the model reacts. By mathematically comparing the model’s behavior across these scenarios, we calculate a precise score that indicates the magnitude of the model’s dependence on irrelevant patterns. This metric allows to put a concrete number on a model’s trustworthiness and ensuring that medical decisions are driven by biology, not background noise.

title: Clustering improves support vector machines classification performance even without the kernel trick
abstract: With suitable kernels and parameters, support vector machines (SVMs) usually outperform other classification methods in terms of accuracy and generalization ability. However, finding appropriate kernels and hyperparameters is time-consuming, especially for large-scale classification tasks. In this paper, we demonstrate that clustering—when designed with classification in mind—can effectively replace kernelization. We propose a novel class-aware clustering method, SEKmeans, which jointly optimizes intra-cluster compactness, cluster purity, and intra-cluster linear separability within a unified objective. This design explicitly facilitates downstream linear classification and enables linear classifiers to capture nonlinear patterns without using any kernel function.We conduct extensive comparisons with linear SVM, linear Twin-SVM (TWSVM), kernel SVM, kernel Twin-SVM, the clustering-based CSVM, and two K-means-based counterparts of SVM and TWSVM, namely K_SVM and K_TWSVM. Experimental results show that our SEKmeans-based variants of SVM and TWSVM(SEK_SVM and SEK_TWSVM) achieve competitive accuracy and F1-scores comparable to those of kernel-based methods, while requiring substantially less computational time.

title: Dynamic Adaptation of the LLM Context for Generating Routines with Coupled Semantics
abstract: LLM-based code generation fails when correctness depends on execution-dependent coupling: the meaning of one routine is defined by the runtime behavior of another, a relationship that cannot be resolved from textual descriptions alone. This limitation, which we call static binding, is not confined to explicitly coupled problems; it appears to varying degrees whenever correctness depends on joint execution behavior across components, from explicit cross-coupled optimizers to subtler joint constraints in packing, routing, and symbolic search. This paper proposes dynamic context adaptation, a sample-efficient validation-generation loop designed for this setting. A validation agent extracts structured diagnostic information from execution traces, providing gradient-like guidance to a generation agent that proposes multiple candidates per iteration. A knowledge graph derived from the problem description supplies semantic constraints to the generation agent. Simulated annealing selects among candidates to avoid greedy collapse. Our method outperforms zero-shot, Reflexion, and OpenEvolve on seven of eight problems at both 300 and 600 evaluations (p < 0.01), a regime where population-based search has not yet accumulated sufficient diversity to compete. Notably, on the primary motivating problem (cross-coupled optimization), our method also achieves the best score at 1000 evaluations, consistent with the hypothesis that structured execution feedback is most beneficial when correctness depends on runtime coupling. Ablation results confirm that structured execution feedback is the primary driver.

title: Data-Driven Learning of Unknown Nonlinear Differential Equations Using Functional Analysis
abstract: In this paper, the problem of data-driven discovery of nonlinear ordinary differential equations (ODEs) is recast, and a new interpretable machine learning (ML) method is proposed. The proposed method aims to learn the unknown vector field of nonlinear dynamics without prior knowledge of the system's physics from only one single state trajectory's data. The proposed method has two fundamental differences with existing methods: 1) the formulation presented in this method is derived based on Functional Analysis and Operator Theory, and 2) the cost function is constructed in the function space as a distance between two functions as an integral, instead of the discrete-sum of errors used in existing ML approaches. An incremental learning algorithm is proposed to learn the unknown vector field to handle new training samples in an online manner. The proposed method can discover the unknown vector field from both forced and unforced autonomous and non-autonomous (or time-varying) dynamical systems. The proposed method is able to simultaneously discover unknown external forces as a function of time and unknown underlying dynamics. Finally, numerical examples are given to demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method.

title: Sparse auto-regressive modeling for scene generation from multi-view images
abstract: Generating complete 3D scenes from sparse, unconstrained views is a fundamental challenge in 3D vision which requires reasoning beyond observed content while remaining computationally tractable. Existing feed-forward reconstruction methods are inherently limited to content visible in the input images, while 3D generative modeling is hindered by the high computational cost of dense volumetric representations and the scarcity of large-scale 3D supervision. We introduce SPAR3S, a sparse voxel-aligned 3D latent generative model for conditional scene completion without requiring ground-truth 3D data for supervision. Our key insight is to formulate 3D scene generation in a structured, compact, voxel-aligned 3D latent space where only occupied voxels are represented. We learn this sparse latent space directly from multi-view images using photometric supervision via differentiable 3D Gaussian Splatting. Given a partial set of observed voxels encoded from sparse input views, scene completion reduces to predicting the missing latent tokens and their spatial support within the voxel grid. To this end, we train a masked autoregressive transformer that jointly models voxel occupancy and latent token values, enabling efficient and spatially consistent generation of unseen regions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on synthetic indoor scenes, achieving higher novel-view quality than prior work. We further validate its generalization on RealEstate10k, highlighting its applicability to real-world data.

title: Markovian Shock-Source Tracing and Multidimensional Asset Roles in Exchange Rates, Gold Futures, and Bitcoin
abstract: This study examines cross-asset connectedness in an international financial network of major exchange rates, gold futures, and Bitcoin. Moving beyond the conventional net transmitter--receiver classification, we characterize asset roles through three complementary dimensions: direct spillover transmission, stationary source-tracing dynamics, and multistep upstream connectivity. Return spillovers are estimated using VAR generalized forecast-error variance decomposition (VAR-GFEVD). A stationary departure flux describes long-run movement in this source-tracing chain, while Viral Centrality is evaluated by the deterministic probability-propagation algorithm of Fink et al. to approximate multistep upstream reach. Empirically, gold futures emerge as the dominant direct net transmitter and the leading stationary source-tracing node, but do not have the largest Viral Centrality. Several exchange-rate nodes classified as direct net receivers have relatively high Viral Centrality, indicating broad conditional access to upstream source nodes. Bitcoin occupies an intermediate role. An auxiliary specification including the U.S. Dollar Index yields qualitatively similar role differentiation. The results show that direct connectedness, stationary source tracing, and approximate multistep upstream reach cannot be inferred from NET spillovers alone. title: Spectral Convergence of Random Feature Method in Multiple Dimensions
abstract: We first prove spectral convergence of the random feature method (RFM) for multidimensional targets in Sobolev, Gevrey, ultra-analytic, and bandlimited classes. The analysis establishes general high-probability approximation estimates in the interpolation scale generated by a kernel integral operator. On a single event determined only by the sampled features, one random space approximates every target in a prescribed source ball; moreover, for each target, a single coefficient vector defines an approximant that attains spectral accuracy simultaneously in all admissible error norms. For both regularity-adapted frequency distributions and uniform distributions on growing frequency windows, the resulting rates range from super-exponential to algebraic, depending on the regularity of the target. Second, we establish abstract error estimates for strong- and weak-form RFM discretizations, thereby converting the preceding approximation bounds into convergence estimates for multidimensional second-order elliptic boundary value and eigenvalue problems. Finally, for random feature matrices (RFMtxs), we prove super-exponential singular-value decay with Fourier features and exponential decay with $\tanh$ features, together with corresponding condition-number lower bounds. The analysis identifies a common mechanism: the same spectral approximation that yields high accuracy also drives severe ill-conditioning.
