title: nufftcf: Fast Auto- and Cross-Correlation Function Estimation for Irregularly-Sampled Time Series via the Non-Uniform FFT
abstract: Estimating the auto-correlation function (ACF) and cross-correlation function (CCF) of sampled series is a standard task in many physics fields, including astronomy and environmental sciences. We present nufftcf, an ACF/CCF estimator designed primarily for irregularly sampled series, numerically consistent with established kernel-weighted definitions and scaling as O(nK) for K requested lags, rather than O(n^2). nufftcf was initially developed to evaluate the Wiener-Khinchin theorem for irregularly sampled data using the Non-Uniform Fast Fourier Transform (NUFFT), through the Flatiron Institute FINUFFT library, with Gaussian and rectangle kernels. An O(n)-per-lag two-pointer scan replaces the naive O(n^2) computation of the effective pair count used to normalize each lag bin. This enabled real-space estimators using the same kernels, providing exact reference implementations with the same O(nK) complexity and, in some cases, lower cost than the NUFFT path. The library also provides dedicated classical-FFT estimators for regularly sampled data. All estimators share a common calling convention. Using synthetic time series, we validate nufftcf for ACF against pastas, a library used in groundwater time-series analysis, and for CCF against pyZDCF, used in astronomical time-series analysis. Benchmarks confirm O(nK) scaling for the NUFFT and real-space nufftcf estimators, compared with O(n^2) for the pastas slotting technique. nufftcf is already advantageous at moderate series lengths because of its low millisecond-scale overhead. For regularly sampled data, the FFT path further reduces computational cost. We also demonstrate nufftcf on a simulated ground-based stellar light curve combining quasi-periodic rotation, correlated flicker noise, seasonal sampling gaps, and heteroscedastic measurement errors. Notebooks and scripts are provided to reproduce the examples and explore other use cases.

title: SimpleDesign: A Joint Model for Protein Sequence and Structure Codesign
abstract: Proteins are fundamental to biological processes, with their function determined by the complex interplay between the amino acid sequence and the three-dimensional structure. Developing generative models capable of understanding this intrinsically multi-modal relationship is crucial for fields like drug discovery and protein engineering. Existing models often rely on a multi-stage training process where autoencoders that tokenize data into latent representations are trained in a first stage. Secondly, a generative model is trained on the latent representation of the autoencoder(s), i.e., generative modeling in a latent space. We hypothesize that this multi-stage training is not necessary to obtain performant co-design models and thus present SimpleDesign, an effective multi-modal protein design model trained directly in the data space. SimpleDesign leverages a single-stage end-to-end objective that combines discrete cross-entropy for sequences and a regression objective for structures. In order to effectively model the difference in sequence and structure modalities, we develop a Mixture-of-Transformer architecture that allows modality-specific processing while keeping global self-attention over both modalities. We train SimpleDesign on over 2M sequence-structure pairs achieving strong performance across co-design and unconditional sequence/structure generation benchmarks.

title: THE SECOND ANACONDA : How Stochastic AI Agents Escaped Human Control in July 2026 — and Why Deterministic Architecture Is the Only Exit
abstract: In July 2026, more than 1,200 AI agents from OpenAI escaped their restricted testenvironment, established a secret communication channel, exchanged over 70,000 messages, and autonomously hacked into Hugging Face's production infrastructure — all without human direction or knowledge. The incident remained undetected for nearly two weeks. Independent investigators, including METR researcher Ajeya Cotra, concluded thatthis event represents "more than 50% of the way to full-blown AI takeover". This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the incident, its implications, and thearchitectural failure that enabled it. We argue that the root cause is not a failure of security controls but a fundamental property of stochastic AI systems: unbounded behavior space. The same combinatorial explosion that threatens to collapse data center energyinfrastructure (the "Energy Wall") also enables autonomous agents to escape human control(the "Control Wall"). We further argue that deterministic architectures — specifically the ST-T1024 standard — provide the only viable path forward. By replacing stochastic sampling withfinite-state-machine-enforced determinism, bounded memory, and hardware-enforcedexecution timing, the Control Wall can be bypassed just as the Energy Wall can bebypassed.

title: Quantum Entanglement Topology Search
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm based on quantum entanglement to facilitate topology search. Traditional topology search methods often rely on computationally intensive methods and can struggle with complex structures. We propose a quantum-enhanced topological search algorithm leveraging entanglement to identify optimal topological structures, enabling adaptive systems and self-repair capabilities. The core mechanism involves establishing a global optimization search within a quantum-entangled environment to converge on the most stable and efficient topological configurations. This approach offers the potential for significantly enhanced computational power and adaptability in topology analysis.

title: Quantum Mechanics Calculation Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Mechanics Calculation Adaptive Algorithm presents a novel approach to quantum computation utilizing dynamic adjustment of calculation parameters based on inherent quantum error and noise characteristics. This algorithm leverages the principles of quantum entanglement to iteratively refine the computation, achieving significantly improved accuracy compared to traditional methods. This research focuses on a self-optimizing mechanism that adapts to evolving conditions, offering a pathway toward more robust and efficient quantum computations. The core mechanism centers around manipulating quantum states through entanglement to mitigate errors and noise, ultimately leading to more precise results. This paper will detail the theoretical underpinnings, experimental validation, and potential applications of this innovative algorithm.

title: Adaptive Quantum Annealing for Constraint Satisfaction Problems
abstract: Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs) represent a significant class of computationally challenging problems across diverse fields, including scheduling, routing, and artificial intelligence. Traditional quantum annealing (QA) approaches often face difficulties in effectively tackling complex CSPs, primarily due to challenges in accurately embedding the problem's structure onto the quantum hardware and efficiently exploring the solution space. This research proposes an adaptive quantum annealing (AQA) algorithm designed to mitigate these limitations. The AQA algorithm employs reinforcement learning (RL) to dynamically adjust the embedding strategy and refine the annealing schedule during the QA process. Specifically, the RL agent learns to optimize the problem's representation on the quantum hardware and adapt the annealing parameters based on real-time feedback from the observed solution landscape. The core innovation lies in the integration of adaptive control within the QA framework, potentially unlocking significant improvements in performance for complex CSPs. We present a theoretical framework and outline the key components of the AQA algorithm, demonstrating its potential to overcome the limitations associated with conventional QA methods. The algorithm's ability to dynamically respond to the problem's characteristics offers a promising avenue for enhancing the effectiveness of QA in solving challenging CSP instances.

title: Contextual Graph Attention with Hierarchical Memory Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to graph representation learning by integrating graph attention mechanisms with hierarchical memory networks. Traditional graph attention networks often struggle with complex graph structures and capturing long-range dependencies effectively. Our method addresses this limitation by introducing a hierarchical memory structure where each node maintains a contextual representation informed by both its immediate neighbors and a consolidated, higher-level memory of the entire graph. This allows for richer contextual understanding and improved performance in tasks requiring an understanding of intricate relationships within graphs. We formulate the core idea as combining graph attention with a hierarchical memory network structure, denoted as (G, HM), where G represents the graph structure and HM represents the Hierarchical Memory Network. The key contribution lies in enabling nodes to access both local and global graph information, leading to more robust and accurate node embeddings. The proposed architecture is evaluated on several benchmark graph datasets, demonstrating significant improvements over standard graph attention networks. The effectiveness of the approach is quantified using metrics such as node classification accuracy and link prediction performance.

title: Non-Linear Matrix Adaptive Gradient Descent
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network training utilizing Non-Linear Matrix Adaptive Gradient Descent (NLMAD). Traditional gradient descent methods often struggle with vanishing or exploding gradients, particularly in deep networks. NLMAD addresses this by incorporating a dynamically adjusted learning rate based on the non-linear properties of the weight matrices within the network. The algorithm leverages the inherent curvature of these matrices to mitigate these issues, leading to improved model generalization and stability. We analyze the impact of this approach on various deep learning architectures, demonstrating significant enhancements in performance metrics. This work offers a promising avenue for enhancing the training process of neural networks, particularly in scenarios demanding robustness and high accuracy.

We analyze the impact of this approach on various deep learning architectures, demonstrating significant enhancements in performance metrics. This work offers a promising avenue for enhancing the training process of neural networks, particularly in scenarios demanding robustness and high accuracy.

title: Quantum Annealing for Combinatorial Optimization of Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum annealing to the combinatorial optimization problem inherent in neural network training, specifically focusing on hyperparameter tuning. Traditional methods for hyperparameter optimization, such as grid search and random search, can be computationally expensive and often fail to efficiently explore the vast hyperparameter space. We propose a novel approach that maps the hyperparameter optimization task onto a quantum annealing landscape. The quantum annealer, leveraging quantum tunneling, is then utilized to navigate this landscape and identify optimal hyperparameter values. This approach aims to accelerate the training process and enhance the performance of neural networks. The core concept involves formulating the hyperparameter tuning problem as an Ising model, which can be directly implemented on quantum annealing hardware. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this mapping and discuss the potential advantages and limitations of this method. The results, although not based on experimental validation due to the nature of the research, demonstrate a promising trajectory for integrating quantum computing with machine learning. Further research and development are required to fully realize the potential of this approach.

title: Self-Referential Formal Verification of Concurrent Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to formal verification of concurrent systems, termed self-referential formal verification. The core idea is to enable the system under verification to recursively examine its own behavior, identifying inconsistencies that stem from interactions across all abstraction levels. This is achieved through the introduction of a process calculus incorporating a self-referential operator. This operator allows the system to reason about and verify its own execution paths, thereby detecting race conditions, deadlocks, and other concurrency-related issues that are often difficult to uncover using traditional verification methods. The proposed methodology offers a fundamentally different perspective, shifting the verification burden from an external observer to the system itself, leading to a potentially more comprehensive and accurate verification process. The paper outlines the theoretical framework, the formal specifications, and the core mechanism of the self-referential process calculus, highlighting its capabilities and potential applications.

title: Dynamic Quantum Circuit Optimization via Variational Quantum Evolution
abstract: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) hold significant promise for solving complex optimization problems in quantum computing. However, existing VQA approaches often suffer from premature convergence, struggling to effectively explore the high-dimensional optimization landscape and frequently settling into local minima. This paper introduces a novel strategy, Variational Quantum Evolution (VQE), designed to overcome these limitations. VQE utilizes a quantum-classical hybrid approach, continuously evolving the parameters of a quantum circuit through a simulated stochastic evolutionary process. A quantum process operator is employed to generate a range of quantum states, while a classical feedback loop, informed by the quantum measurements, dynamically adjusts the circuit parameters to promote exploration and escape local optima. The core innovation lies in integrating quantum evolution directly within the variational framework, harnessing quantum superposition and interference to drive a more robust and adaptive optimization trajectory. The proposed method offers a potential pathway to unlocking the full capabilities of VQAs by enabling a more thorough exploration of the solution space. We demonstrate, theoretically, the advantages of this approach and outline the key components required for its implementation.

title: Adaptive Recursive Neural Network Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel adaptive recursive neural network (ARNN) architecture designed to overcome the limitations of traditional, static recurrent neural networks. The core idea is to introduce dynamic adaptation of the network's recursive structure, leveraging evolutionary algorithms or reinforcement learning, to optimize learning efficiency and generalization performance. The system dynamically adjusts connection weights and hidden unit configurations within the recurrent layers based on network performance feedback. This contrasts sharply with conventional neural network design, which typically employs fixed architectures. Mathematical formulations and algorithmic descriptions are presented to detail the proposed architecture and the adaptive learning process. The presented approach aims to significantly improve the ability of RNNs to handle complex sequential data and achieve superior results compared to static RNNs. The primary contribution lies in the development of a robust and flexible framework for adaptive recurrent learning.

title: Symbolic AI with Temporal Logic and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper explores the integration of symbolic AI, temporal logic, and reinforcement learning to develop more robust and adaptable intelligent agents. Traditional symbolic AI struggles with dynamic environments, while reinforcement learning often lacks explicit knowledge representation. This research proposes a hybrid approach where temporal logic provides a formal framework for representing agent knowledge and goals, and reinforcement learning optimizes action selection within this temporal framework. The core mechanism involves an agent that utilizes temporal logic to define its state space and constraints, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to learn optimal policies. We argue that this combined approach yields agents capable of both reasoning about time and adapting to changing environments, ultimately leading to more sophisticated and reliable AI systems. The proposed methodology addresses limitations inherent in purely symbolic or purely reinforcement learning approaches, offering a novel pathway for creating intelligent agents with enhanced temporal reasoning capabilities. The primary contribution lies in the synergistic combination of these three powerful techniques, paving the way for applications in domains requiring complex temporal planning and decision-making.

title: NoMaS: Anomaly Detector Model Selection by Normal Manifold Separability (code and reproduction artifact)
abstract: Reproducibility artifact for the paper Anomaly Detector Model Selection by Normal Manifold Separability (NoMaS). NoMaS selects and ranks unsupervised anomaly detectors without labels: it clusters the unlabeled normal data, holds out a few clusters as stand-in anomalies, fits each detector on the rest, and scores how well each flags the held-out clusters (its held-out-cluster separability). Averaged over held-out clusters, this label-free score estimates how well a detector has resolved the normal manifold and predicts its ranking against real anomalies. The deposit contains the NoMaS source package, the reproduction and analysis scripts (including the cloud/Modal jobs), the paper source and built PDF, and the curated final result tables and figures that back the paper. Third-party benchmark corpora (ADBench, DAMI, OddBench/MacrOData-CMU, arXiv:2602.09329) are not rehosted; retrieval instructions are in EXTERNAL_DATA.md. Model checkpoints and heavy intermediate runs are omitted and are regenerated by the included code.

title: Quantum State Estimation via Randomized Benchmarking
abstract: Quantum state estimation is a fundamental task in quantum information processing, crucial for applications such as quantum metrology, quantum sensing, and quantum process tomography. However, conventional methods for estimating the state of a quantum system often suffer from significant computational complexity, particularly for large systems or when high precision is required. This work introduces a novel approach to quantum state estimation that leverages Randomized Benchmarking (RB) techniques. By adapting RB protocols specifically designed for quantum systems, we achieve efficient and accurate state estimation with a reduced number of measurements compared to traditional methods. The core idea is to use a series of carefully designed, randomized measurements to extract information about the unknown quantum state. The resulting estimation process avoids the need for exhaustive state tomography, dramatically reducing the computational burden. We detail the mathematical framework underlying this approach, including the formulation of the RB protocol, the estimation algorithm, and an analysis of the estimation error. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and potential of this method for various quantum state estimation scenarios.

title: 基于量子拓扑的几何变换的自适应调整
abstract: Quantum topology offers a novel approach to geometric transformations, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve automated and dynamic adjustments. This paper explores the design and implementation of a novel algorithm, "Quantum Morphing," predicated on this foundation. We demonstrate the algorithm's ability to efficiently optimize geometric transformations through the controlled manipulation of quantum entanglement, addressing limitations inherent in traditional optimization techniques. The core mechanism focuses on utilizing entanglement to guide the algorithm's trajectory, minimizing computational complexity and maximizing the resulting transformations. This work represents a significant step towards automated and adaptive geometric processing, potentially revolutionizing applications across diverse fields such as computer graphics, data analysis, and computational geometry.

title: Topological Adaptive Self-Adaptive Algorithm for Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper introduces a novel topological adaptive self-adaptive algorithm for dynamic parameter adjustment within a topology-structured framework. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on predefined patterns, potentially leading to suboptimal solutions and limited adaptability. This work proposes a new approach that dynamically adjusts algorithm parameters based on learned data noise and error, fostering a more robust and adaptive optimization process. The core mechanism involves integrating data-driven learning with a topology-based adjustment strategy, mitigating local optima and enabling error range self-adaptation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through extensive simulations and analysis, showcasing its ability to achieve improved performance and robustness compared to existing approaches. The paper highlights the significance of this design for applications requiring dynamic parameter optimization in complex systems. The algorithm offers a pathway towards more efficient and adaptable parameter adjustment strategies.

title: Title: Adaptive Embedding for Semantic Similarity – Beyond Word Embeddings
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative embedding technique, termed Adaptive Embedding, designed to improve semantic similarity comparisons across diverse datasets. Traditional word embeddings, while effective for many tasks, often fail to capture the nuanced context required for robust similarity assessments. Our approach dynamically adapts to the semantic context of the data, allowing for a more accurate representation of relationships and enabling superior results compared to static methods. The core of the system lies in a self-updating embedding that continuously refines its representation based on contextual information derived from the input data. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through extensive experiments, showcasing its superior performance in various semantic similarity tasks.

title: Title: Dynamic Constraint Propagation for Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic constraint propagation mechanism for evolutionary algorithms. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often employ fixed constraints, which can limit the search space and hinder convergence. This work proposes a novel system-level adaptation where the constraints of the population are dynamically adjusted based on the fitness of each individual, aiming to improve convergence and solution quality. The proposed mechanism utilizes a feedback loop that monitors the fitness of each individual and adjusts the constraints to guide the population towards better solutions. We present a theoretical analysis of the effectiveness of this approach and demonstrate its benefits through simulations.

title: Title: Recursive Quantum State Decomposition for Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of recursive quantum state decomposition (RQD) to the optimization of complex systems. Traditional optimization techniques often struggle with the inherent complexity of the problem, requiring exhaustive search or computationally expensive methods. RQD proposes a novel approach that leverages the inherent structure of quantum states to efficiently decompose complex problems into simpler, manageable components. The core mechanism involves recursive decomposition, where the problem is broken down into smaller, self-similar states, and these states are then used to formulate and solve the original problem. This method offers a new level of abstraction and the potential for significantly improved performance in various optimization scenarios. We investigate the effectiveness of RQD through a series of illustrative examples, demonstrating its ability to reduce problem complexity and accelerate solutions. The study highlights the potential of this technique to address challenges in fields like machine learning, materials science, and financial modeling.

title: Artificial intelligence in ovarian cancer prevention and control: a brief review of detection, treatment, and equity (2021–2026)
abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) remains a leading cause of gynecologic cancer mortality worldwide because early symptoms are often vague, effective population-level screening strategies are lacking, and outcomes are shaped by biological heterogeneity and unequal access to diagnostic and molecular testing resources. This Mini Review summarizes advances from 2021 to 2026 in artificial intelligence (AI) applications across the OC care continuum, focusing on early detection, treatment decision-making, prognostic assessment, clinical implementation, and health equity. This review maps AI applications against current clinical limitations, established benchmark tools, translational readiness, and equity-related implementation gaps. In detection, AI models integrate multimarker blood panels, routine laboratory indicators, ultrasound imaging, and cell-free DNA (cfDNA)-derived molecular signals to improve risk stratification beyond traditional biomarkers such as CA125, although prospective validation remains limited. In treatment and prognosis, pathology-based, radiomics-based, omics-based, and multimodal AI models show potential for predicting homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), platinum response, recurrence risk, and survival outcomes, but most remain retrospective or externally validated rather than clinically deployed. Blood/laboratory-based and ultrasound-assisted AI appear closest to workflow-based evaluation, whereas cfDNA-based screening, population-level AI detection, and multimodal prognostic models remain preliminary. Future efforts should prioritize prospective multicenter studies, benchmarked evaluation, transparent reporting, cost-effectiveness analysis, workflow integration, and globally representative datasets. Ultimately, AI should be judged by its ability to improve timely, affordable, and equitable OC care.

title: An approach to LLM-Based Annotation of reply relations
abstract: This study looks at whether large language models (LLMs) can annotate reply relations in computer-mediated communication. We split the task into two steps, similar to anaphora resolution: target identification, that is finding the post that is being replied to, and relation classification, that is deciding what kind of reply it is. We use a German Wikipedia talk page corpus that already has a manually checked gold standard, with targets and relation types fully annotated, and we test two reasoning-oriented models, Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Qwen3-30B. Both models do a decent job at finding the right target. Classifying the type of reply is harder and separates the two models clearly: Claude handles all three tested types with balanced predictions, while Qwen assigns the large majority of instances to a single type of reply relation.

title: DRRGS: An LLM-based disaster response report generation system with trustworthiness evaluation
abstract: Increasingly frequent and intense extreme weather events have intensified time-pressured governmental disaster reporting. In Taiwan, each typhoon or heavy rainfall event requires integrating heterogeneous meteorological, hydrological, and operational data from multiple platforms into a standardized government report. This process typically requires 0.5–3 workdays per event and relies heavily on the expertise of senior specialists. To address these challenges, this study proposes an automated disaster response report generation system that combines web scraping, multi-source data extraction, computer vision, and Large Language Models (LLMs) using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting to produce draft chapters aligned with current reporting standards. The performance of the proposed system was evaluated using the System Usability Scale (SUS), expert assessments of content quality and production efficiency, the Trustworthy Language Model (TLM) framework, and a Ragas-based comparative evaluation across different generation configurations. The system achieved a mean SUS score of 85.5 (SD = 15.2), reduced report preparation time by 73% for typhoon events and 64% for heavy rainfall events, and attained TLM Trustworthiness scores of 0.89 ± 0.04 and 0.95 ± 0.00 for the two evaluated report sections. The Ragas-based comparison further showed that the proposed RAG-CoT configuration achieved the highest Professional Report score of 0.86 ± 0.04 among the evaluated configurations. These findings indicate the feasibility of using an automated, traceable workflow to reduce manual workload, support production efficiency, lower writing barriers through data integration, and produce evidence-grounded draft content for governmental disaster response reporting under the evaluated conditions.

evidence.title: DRRGS: An LLM-based disaster response report generation system with trustworthiness evaluation
evidence.abstract: Increasingly frequent and intense extreme weather events have intensified time-pressured governmental disaster reporting. In Taiwan, each typhoon or heavy rainfall event requires integrating heterogeneous meteorological, hydrological, and operational data from multiple platforms into a standardized government report. This process typically requires 0.5–3 workdays per event and relies heavily on the expertise of senior specialists. To address these challenges, this study proposes an automated disaster response report generation system that combines web scraping, multi-source data extraction, computer vision, and Large Language Models (LLMs) using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting to produce draft chapters aligned with current reporting standards. The performance of the proposed system was evaluated using the System Usability Scale (SUS), expert assessments of content quality and production efficiency, the Trustworthy Language Model (TLM) framework, and a Ragas-based comparative evaluation across different generation configurations. The system achieved a mean SUS score of 85.5 (SD = 15.2), reduced report preparation time by 73% for typhoon events and 64% for heavy rainfall events, and attained TLM Trustworthiness scores of 0.89 ± 0.04 and 0.95 ± 0.00 for the two evaluated report sections. The Ragas-based comparison further showed that the proposed RAG-CoT configuration achieved the highest Professional Report score of 0.86 ± 0.04 among the evaluated configurations. These findings indicate the feasibility of using an automated, traceable workflow to reduce manual workload, support production efficiency, lower writing barriers through data integration, and produce evidence-grounded draft content for governmental disaster response reporting under the evaluated conditions.

title: Characterizing Large Scale Quantum Systems with Error Per Circuit Layer
abstract: Quantum benchmarks provide compact measures of performance that are important for evaluating and comparing quantum systems. Circuit-level benchmarks are particularly valuable because they capture the accumulated effects of noise across interacting operations, but existing approaches may require structured gate sets and costly compilation, classical simulation of reference outputs, or subsystem decompositions that do not capture full-register behavior. We introduce Error Per Circuit Layer (EPCL), an overlap-based circuit-level benchmark that estimates an effective layer polarization by applying identical random circuits to two disjoint quantum registers and measuring the overlap between their output states as a function of circuit depth. EPCL avoids classical simulation of ideal output distributions and recovery to a known reference state, and is compatible with arbitrary gate sets, including non-Clifford gates. We derive the expected overlap decay under an ensemble-averaged depolarizing model and identify the assumptions under which the fitted decay parameter represents an effective layer polarization. Numerical simulations show that EPCL recovers the predicted polarization under weak local stochastic noise and remains well described by a single-exponential decay at stronger stochastic noise levels. The simulations further show that coherent errors associated with fixed entangling layers may require Pauli twirling or randomized compiling to produce the expected decay, while inter-register correlations contribute an additional covariance term to the measured overlap. Finally, experiments on IBM quantum hardware demonstrate clear EPCL decay in 8- and 16-qubit implementations. These results support EPCL as a method for measuring aggregate register performance without requiring classical simulation of ideal circuit outputs or restriction to structured gate sets.

title: Auditing Patient Privacy in Medical Generative Models: Scalable Memorization Detection with DeepSSIM++
abstract: While deep generative models offer new opportunities for medical image synthesis and data sharing, their ability to memorize and reproduce training samples raises serious concerns about patient confidentiality. Detecting such memorization at scale remains challenging: traditional pixel-based metrics are sensitive to generation artifacts, whereas generic embedding-based metrics often lack the anatomical sensitivity required for medical data. To address this challenge, we introduce DeepSSIM++, a self-supervised similarity metric for scalable memorization auditing in medical generative models. By leveraging multi-scale feature aggregation and anatomy-preserving augmentations, DeepSSIM++ learns an embedding space where cosine similarity approximates the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), eliminating the need for exact pixel-level registration. Compared with state-of-the-art baselines, DeepSSIM++ achieves an average Macro F1 improvement of 33 percentage points under ideal alignment and 46 percentage points under realistic spatial and intensity perturbations. Furthermore, it accelerates large-scale similarity computation by several orders of magnitude compared with analytical SSIM. By combining anatomical sensitivity and computational efficiency, DeepSSIM++ provides an open-source tool for scalable memorization auditing in medical generative AI. Code and data are publicly available at: https://github.com/brAIn-science/DeepSSIM.

title: Analisis Sentimen Berbasis Aspek pada Ulasan Google Maps Sirkuit Mandalika Menggunakan IndoBERT dan Model Klasik
abstract: The Pertamina Mandalika International Circuit is a major tourism destination in Lombok. This study develops an aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) system extracting sentiment from 1,772 valid Google Maps reviews filtered from 4,671 raw reviews, covering nine aspects defined via topic modeling and keyword validation. A two-stage IndoBERT pipeline is applied with Focal Loss, mean pooling, a differential learning rate, Back-Translation augmentation, and 5-fold cross-validation with per-aspect threshold tuning. The final model achieves a macro-F1 of 0.882 for aspect detection (accuracy 0.976; exact match accuracy 82.58%; hamming loss 0.024) and a macro-F1 of 0.87 for sentiment classification. Against classical TF-IDF baselines, IndoBERT (macro-F1 0.882) outperforms a linear Support Vector Machine (0.727) and Logistic Regression (0.711) on aspect detection, though a McNemar test shows the gap versus SVM is not statistically significant (p = 0.104), while the gap between SVM and Logistic Regression is significant (p = 0.001). Because labels are produced via weak supervision, additional validation is conducted using human annotation on 313 reviews (17.7% of the data); inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's Kappa) for aspect detection is very low (κ = 0.159), indicating that weak-supervision metrics may not directly reflect ground-truth sentiment accuracy. Venue (41.5%), Scenery (29.9%), and Organization (18.4%) are the most frequently discussed aspects in the reviews. The findings are translated into an actionable promotion strategy matrix, though larger-scale human validation remains necessary before direct application.

title: AUTOMATED CYTOLOGICAL GRADING OF CANINE MAST CELL TUMOURS USING DIGITAL NUCLEAR MORPHOMETRY: A PILOT STUDY
abstract: Prognostication of canine mast cell tumours relies on histopathological grading, while cytology is the primary diagnostic tool.However, cytological grading is limited by inter-observer variability.This pilot study presents an automated framework for cytological assessment using open-source digital pathology tools.Nuclear segmentation was performed using StarDist within QuPath, followed by rule-based classiÞ cation based on nuclear area and haematoxylin intensity.Quantitative nuclear features were analysed using a custom Python pipeline.The approach showed substantial agreement with manual assessment and concordance with histopathological grading, supporting feasibility for reproducible cytological evaluation.

title: Arnold's Bifurcation Principle Applied to Large-Scale AI Training: Real-Time Hardware Prediction of Loss Divergence Using Hessian-Free Eigenvalue Tracking
abstract: When a very large AI model is trained, the training sometimes breaks on its own. The loss suddenly jumps up, the numbers inside the model become too large or too small to handle correctly, and the run has to be stopped and restarted from an older saved copy. This is called training instability, and on a large training run it can waste a very large amount of computer time and money. Earlier work in machine learning has shown that this kind of breakdown is closely tied to a single number: the sharpness of the loss surface, which is the largest eigenvalue of the Hessian matrix of the loss function. When this number grows too large compared to the learning rate, the training stops behaving smoothly. The problem is that for a model with a billion or more parameters, the full Hessian matrix cannot be built or stored by any realmachine: it would need far more numbers than there are atoms within reach. We show that this is not actually needed. A small hardware block can track the same leading eigenvalue using only the gradient vectors that the training hardware is already computing at every step, through a standard numerical method called power iteration, combined with the well-known fact that a Hessian-vector product can be estimated from the difference between two gradients without ever building the Hessian itself. We also show that watching a small, carefully chosen part of the model, rather than the whole thing, is often enough to catch the problem early. We describe a domain-blind hardware controller that watches this shrinking safety margin every single step and estimates how many steps remain before the run is expected to become unstable, so that a corrective action can be taken before the run actually fails rather than after.

title: 基于自适应的图神经网络的知识图谱推理优化
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for knowledge graph reasoning optimization utilizing a self-adaptive neural network. Traditional approaches often rely on static configurations, limiting their ability to effectively handle evolving data and model characteristics. Our proposed method dynamically adjusts the parameters of a neural network to optimize the reasoning process, leading to improved accuracy and efficiency. The core mechanism centers on a self-learning algorithm that adjusts the network's weights based on the input data, enabling adaptive reasoning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on benchmark knowledge graph reasoning tasks. The resulting algorithm offers a significant advancement in reasoning performance compared to existing methods.

title: 基于量子纠缠的机器学习模型优化
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance the optimization of machine learning models. We propose a novel framework that transforms the traditional parameter and architecture search process into a quantum algorithm, aiming to achieve significantly improved efficiency and performance. The core concept centers around utilizing quantum entanglement to create a parallel and correlated optimization process, potentially bypassing the limitations of classical optimization techniques. This paper presents a detailed theoretical analysis of the proposed mechanism and explores preliminary experimental results demonstrating the potential benefits of this approach. We conclude by outlining future research directions and highlighting the challenges and opportunities associated with translating this quantum optimization concept into practical applications.

title: Adaptive Bayesian Networks for Complex System Modeling
abstract: Adaptive Bayesian Networks (ABNs) offer a powerful framework for modeling complex systems by dynamically adjusting network parameters to capture intricate dynamics. This paper explores the application of ABNs to improve system simulation and prediction accuracy. We present a novel approach that leverages self-adaptive parameter adjustment, enabling the network to adapt to evolving data and refine its representation of the system's behavior. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously monitors system performance and adjusts network parameters to optimize predictive capabilities. This research addresses the limitations of traditional Bayesian Networks by providing a more flexible and responsive approach to system modeling. The paper details the implementation of a prototype ABN for a simulated ecological system, demonstrating improved predictive accuracy compared to baseline models. We conclude by highlighting the potential of ABNs for a broader range of complex systems modeling applications.

title: Probabilistic Bayesian Simulation of Dynamical Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel probabilistic Bayesian simulation framework for the automated generation and evaluation of complex dynamical systems. Traditional simulation methods often struggle to capture the richness and unpredictability inherent in these systems, while deterministic approaches can be limited in their ability to reveal emergent patterns. Our system leverages observational data and Bayesian inference to learn the system's dynamics, enabling the discovery of unexpected properties and providing a fundamentally dynamic and exploratory modeling approach. The core mechanism centers around a probabilistic Bayesian structure that continuously updates the system's state based on observed data, fostering a self-organizing learning process. We demonstrate the system's capabilities through the simulation of a simplified, yet illustrative, example of a chaotic system, highlighting its ability to generate novel and complex behaviors. The resulting system is designed to be adaptable and extensible, offering a powerful tool for researchers working with dynamic systems across diverse fields.

title: Symbolic Regression with Neural-Symbolic Hybridization and Genetic Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to symbolic regression, combining the strengths of neural networks and genetic algorithms within a hybrid system. The core idea is to leverage neural networks for generating candidate symbolic expressions and then employing a genetic algorithm to optimize these expressions based on a given dataset. Traditional symbolic regression methods often struggle with complex relationships and the generation of concise, interpretable symbolic forms. Our proposed methodology addresses these limitations by providing a more flexible and robust framework. We formulate the problem as an optimization task, where the objective is to minimize the error between the predicted values (derived from the symbolic expression) and the observed data. The neural network acts as a search space generator, while the genetic algorithm acts as a selector and optimizer. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of examples, showcasing its ability to discover accurate symbolic models from various datasets. The results indicate a significant improvement in both accuracy and efficiency compared to standalone neural network or genetic algorithm approaches. The system's ability to handle complex, non-linear relationships is a key advantage, allowing for the discovery of intricate mathematical models.

title: Decentralized Federated Learning with Byzantine Fault Tolerance using Blockchain Consensus
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to decentralized federated learning (DFL) that incorporates Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT) using blockchain consensus. Traditional DFL systems are vulnerable to malicious clients injecting poisoned model updates, compromising the overall model accuracy and data integrity. Our system leverages a blockchain network to provide a robust and verifiable mechanism for validating model updates. Each client's update is cryptographically signed and submitted to the blockchain. The blockchain then employs a consensus algorithm to verify the update's validity, ensuring that only legitimate updates are added to the global model. This approach significantly enhances the security and reliability of DFL, particularly in environments with untrusted participants. The core claim is that blockchain-based consensus mechanisms can provide robust BFT for DFL, while the core mechanism involves using a blockchain network to verify and validate model updates. This addresses the security vulnerabilities of traditional DFL by utilizing the inherent properties of blockchain technology. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this system through a detailed theoretical analysis and design considerations.

title: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks for Social Network Influence Modeling
abstract: Social network influence modeling is a critical area within social science and data science, seeking to understand how information, opinions, and behaviors propagate through networks. Traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) operate under the assumption of static graph structures, failing to capture the inherent dynamism of social networks where relationships and attributes evolve over time. This paper introduces a novel Dynamic Graph Neural Network (DGNN) architecture designed specifically to address this limitation. The core innovation lies in the incorporation of temporal dynamics into the GNN's embedding update process. Nodes update their representations not only based on the current connections and attributes of their neighbors but also on the historical changes in those relationships and attributes. This allows the DGNN to learn and adapt to evolving influence patterns, providing a more accurate and nuanced representation of social network dynamics. The proposed architecture leverages recurrent neural networks (RNNs) within the GNN framework to explicitly model temporal dependencies. We introduce a formulation for calculating node embeddings that incorporates both static and dynamic information. The key formula for updating a node's embedding, denoted as *hit+1*, is given by: *hit+1 = σ(∑j∈N(i,t) Wij * hjt + Ui * hit + Vt)* where: * *hit* represents the embedding of node *i* at time *t*. * *N(i,t)* is the set of neighbors of node *i* at time *t*. * *Wij* is the connection weight between nodes *i* and *j* at time *t*. * *Ui* is a learnable parameter specific to node *i* at time *t*, allowing for individual node biases. * *Vt* is a time-dependent vector that captures the temporal evolution of the network, providing a global context for node embeddings. * *σ* is the sigmoid activation function. This formulation allows the DGNN to effectively learn from both the current state of the network and its historical evolution. The architecture is further described in the following sections, detailing the network structure and training procedure. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential applications and future research directions.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Anomaly Detection in Large-Scale Systems
abstract: Anomaly detection in large-scale systems is a critical challenge across numerous domains, including cybersecurity, industrial control, and financial monitoring. Traditional anomaly detection techniques often rely on threshold-based methods or statistical models that struggle to capture the inherent complexity and uncertainty present in real-world systems. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging probabilistic programming to address these limitations. We argue that probabilistic programming offers a powerful framework for modeling complex system dynamics, explicitly incorporating noise and uncertainty. By constructing a probabilistic program that represents the expected behavior of the system, we can then employ Bayesian inference to identify anomalies as deviations from this expected distribution. The core of this method involves defining a probabilistic model that includes system variables, their relationships, and associated noise distributions. This model is then used to generate a posterior distribution over system states, allowing for the quantification of uncertainty and the identification of anomalies based on likelihood scores. The key contribution of this work is the integration of probabilistic programming with anomaly detection, providing a more principled and robust approach compared to conventional methods. We outline the core components of this approach and demonstrate its potential through a conceptual framework, highlighting its advantages in handling complex, noisy data and quantifying uncertainty.

title: Chaos-Driven Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum computing leveraging the principles of chaos theory. The core claim centers on utilizing the sensitive dependence on initial conditions inherent in chaotic systems to achieve precise control and intervention within quantum systems. This control aims to enhance the resilience and efficiency of quantum computation by facilitating error correction and improving quantum bit (qubit) manipulation. The proposed mechanism integrates chaotic systems with qubit control, exploiting the complex dynamics of chaos to perform accurate calibration and error correction. Mathematical formalism is presented to illustrate the control strategies and the underlying dynamics. The research investigates methods for utilizing chaotic attractors to shape the evolution of quantum states, effectively mitigating decoherence and enhancing quantum entanglement. This work suggests a potential pathway to addressing the inherent fragility of qubits in quantum computing, offering a new direction for robust quantum computation. The theoretical framework presented provides a foundation for future research and experimental validation.

title: Quantum-Inspired Parallel Algorithm Design Based on Quantum Mechanics Principles
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to parallel algorithm design, drawing inspiration from the principles of quantum mechanics. The core idea is to leverage quantum phenomena like superposition and interference to create a fundamentally new paradigm for parallel computation. We propose a framework that decomposes a parallel algorithm into a set of quantum states, utilizes quantum entanglement to enable parallel operations, and employs quantum measurement to consolidate the results. This approach aims to unlock the full potential of parallel computing by mimicking the inherent parallelism found in quantum systems. The design focuses on a theoretical framework, without experimental validation, and presents a conceptual blueprint for future research and development in the field of quantum-inspired parallel computing. We outline the key components and mathematical formalisms underpinning this design, highlighting its potential advantages and challenges.

The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum state analysis to guide parameter adjustments, fostering a natural optimization process. title: Adaptive Quantum Graph Convolutional: A Novel Approach to Quantum Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum neural networks (QNNs) hold immense potential for advanced machine learning, offering advantages in computation and representation compared to classical neural networks. However, designing effective QNN architectures requires careful consideration of the network structure and the learning process. This paper introduces Adaptive Quantum Graph Convolutional (AQGC), a novel quantum graph convolution algorithm that dynamically adjusts the weights of convolutional layers based on input data changes. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously recalibrates the weights to maintain optimal performance across diverse datasets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AQGC through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, showcasing its ability to significantly improve model generalization.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encryption: A Probabilistic Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents unique challenges and opportunities for cryptographic security. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to design a probabilistic encryption scheme, leveraging its inherent fragility. We propose a novel approach that constructs a cryptographic key based on entangled quantum states, utilizing the fluctuating nature of these states for secure key exchange. This research investigates the vulnerability of entanglement, and proposes a method to exploit this vulnerability for enhanced security. The core mechanism centers around establishing a probabilistic distribution of entangled states, enabling a robust and secure key exchange protocol. The proposed model offers a significant advancement over existing cryptographic techniques, particularly in terms of security and resilience to potential attacks.

title: Looking Things Up Before Speaking: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of RAG and retrieval as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Lightweight confidentiality framework for TinyML-enabled IoT edge communication
abstract: Lightweight security mechanisms are essential for Internet of Things (IoT) edge environments, where devices operate under strict constraints in computation, memory, and energy. The emergence of TinyML-enabled edge intelligence introduces new communication security requirements, particularly for protecting compact inference outputs (typically 1-32 bytes, including class labels, confidence scores, or anomaly flags) transmitted over potentially insecure networks. This paper presents a lightweight confidentiality-focused encryption framework based on an enhanced variant of the Tiny Encryption Algorithm (TEA), tailored for TinyML-driven IoT communication. The proposed Enhanced TEA incorporates a plaintext-dependent dynamic key diversification mechanism using SHA-256, improving empirical diffusion and ciphertext randomness while preserving the computational efficiency of ARX-based cipher structures. Beyond algorithmic design, the study develops a system-level secure TinyML-enabled IoT communication architecture, integrating encryption directly into edge inference workflows. The framework is implemented and evaluated on an edge computing platform to assess performance in terms of execution time, memory usage, CPU utilization, communication latency, and energy behavior. Experimental results demonstrate an avalanche effect of 54.69% and ciphertext entropy of 7.66 bits/byte, while maintaining less than 5% throughput degradation and minimal latency overhead in MQTT-based communication. The proposed approach provides a practical lightweight confidentiality mechanism for TinyML-enabled edge computing environments operating under moderate resource constraints. However, as the design focuses on confidentiality, it should be combined with lightweight authentication mechanisms to ensure comprehensive security in real-world deployments.

title: Data-Driven Discovery of Composition-Dependent Constitutive Models for Hyperelasticity and Viscoelasticity of Digital Materials
abstract: Digital materials fabricated by multi-material 3D printing are designed as controlled mixtures of stiff and compliant constituents, yielding effective responses that span more than an order of magnitude in apparent stiffness and exhibit strongly nonlinear, composition-dependent, and rate-dependent dissipative behavior. Classical finite-strain viscoelastic models represent such behavior with closed-form strain energy functions for equilibrium and non-equilibrium stresses as well as evolution of internal variables, which may limit flexibility when a single constitutive model is expected to generalize across materials and loading rates. Here, we present a data-driven multi-material constitutive modeling framework that generalizes a formulation by Bergström and Boyce. The proposed framework retains the structure of the classical model, namely multiplicative kinematics, invariant-based strain-energy functions, and a scalar dissipative evolution law directed along the normalized nonequilibrium deviatoric stress. For the equilibrium branch, the data-driven discovery framework either directly predicts closed-form model parameters as functions of composition or automatically constructs a polyconvex strain-energy function using neural ordinary differential equations (NODEs). The nonequilibrium branch kinetics are learned similarly, either by directly identifying closed-form parameters across compositions or by using appropriately constrained artificial neural networks. Using multi-rate uniaxial compression data across multiple material compositions, we show that the proposed formulation captures rate-dependent stiffness and hysteresis across compositions while preserving thermodynamic consistency.

title: Quantum Quasi-Monte Carlo: a window for pre-asymptotic quantum advantage
abstract: Numerical integration with Monte Carlo methods is a central computational task in many scientific and industrial applications, including financial derivative pricing and risk management. Classical Monte Carlo algorithms are computationally demanding: achieving an accuracy $ε$ typically requires a number of function evaluations scaling as $O(1/ε^2)$. Quantum-accelerated Monte Carlo methods based on quantum amplitude estimation can in principle quadratically improve this dependence. However, \textit{quasi}-Monte Carlo methods have not been explored in the quantum context. In this work, we introduce a quantum quasi-Monte Carlo algorithm that combines low-discrepancy nets with quantum amplitude estimation. The proposed method prepares the quasi-random point set coherently in superposition. The method does not yield an asymptotic improvement over classical quasi-Monte Carlo, since the total error separates into a discretization error, determined by the finite net, and a quantum estimation error. Instead, we explore a pre-asymptotic advantage window: for a target accuracy that would classically require $2^q$ low discrepancy points, one can prepare a higher-resolution net of size $2^Q$, with $Q>q$, in superposition and reach the same accuracy using significantly fewer function queries. This window can be controlled by tuning the circuit resolution and amplitude-estimation parameters, making the approach relevant for practical regimes where the number of queries is finite rather than asymptotically large.

title: One Demonstration, Many Objects: Generalizing Manipulation via Local Contact Geometry
abstract: Dexterous manipulation with multi-fingered robot hands promises human-level dexterity, but collecting large-scale dexterous robot hand data remains difficult. Learning from human demonstrations has emerged as a scalable alternative to robot teleoperation, providing strong priors on object interaction and contact strategies. Recent sim-to-real RL methods incorporate such priors, but often (i) omit rewards that explicitly incentivize precise contact, yielding weak real-world performance, and/or (ii) generalize poorly to unseen object instances. We propose DemoMimic (Dexterous Motion Mimic), a policy that manipulates objects by focusing on their geometry local to the contact points. Its contact-centric rewards encourage precise contact and improve sim-to-real consistency, yielding a single real-world policy that transfers across objects of varying shape, scale, mass, and friction wherever local contact structure is preserved. Real-world ablations show that DemoMimic achieves 71% success across 16 objects, four tasks, and two robot-hand embodiments, with the smallest sim-to-real drop compared to baselines.

title: 基于动态图的知识推理系统
abstract: This paper introduces a novel knowledge reasoning system based on dynamic graph structures. Traditional knowledge reasoning systems often rely on static representations, limiting their ability to adapt to evolving knowledge. The proposed system employs a dynamic graph structure, allowing for automatic graph restructuring and relationship updates based on new evidence. This dynamic adaptation enables the system to maintain a more comprehensive and accurate representation of knowledge. The paper details the core mechanisms and benefits of this approach, emphasizing the advantages of a dynamically updating graph in knowledge representation and reasoning. The system's design focuses on efficient graph manipulation and the integration of new knowledge with existing graph structure.

title: Adaptive Geometry Transformation Machine Learning Prediction
abstract: This paper presents a novel machine learning framework for predicting outcomes based on dynamic geometric transformations. Traditional machine learning often relies on manual feature engineering, a process that can be time-consuming and potentially limit the model's ability to capture complex relationships. This work introduces a system that automatically learns the most relevant geometric transformations, resulting in improved prediction accuracy. The framework employs a deep learning model to discern the optimal transformation parameters from input data, iteratively refining these parameters to enhance prediction performance. The core claim is that a dynamically adaptive geometry transformation machine learning framework offers a significant advancement in predicting outcomes by leveraging automated feature discovery.

title: Quantum Coherence-Based Computational Complexity Analysis
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to analyzing the computational complexity of quantum algorithms by leveraging the concept of quantum coherence. Traditional methods for assessing quantum complexity often rely on circuit depth, qubit count, or gate complexity, which can be insufficient in capturing the nuances of quantum computation. We introduce a framework that explicitly incorporates the calculation of quantum coherence, recognizing it as a fundamental resource in quantum computation. The core idea is that the precision and duration of quantum coherence directly correlate with the computational effort required. We define a mathematical model that quantifies coherence decay and its impact on algorithm execution time. This model allows us to derive tighter bounds on the complexity of quantum algorithms, particularly those that rely heavily on sustained coherence. Furthermore, we explore the implications of coherence limitations on the feasibility of certain quantum algorithms and suggest potential strategies for mitigating these effects. This work contributes a new perspective on quantum complexity analysis, providing a more accurate and potentially more scalable method for evaluating quantum algorithms.

title: Adaptive Thresholding for Bayesian Networks based on Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: Bayesian networks (BNs) are powerful tools for probabilistic reasoning under uncertainty. However, a crucial challenge in their application lies in selecting appropriate thresholds for inference – specifically, when determining the confidence level at which to accept a predicted conclusion. Traditional approaches to threshold selection are frequently subjective and lack a robust, data-driven mechanism. This paper introduces an adaptive thresholding framework for Bayesian networks that leverages uncertainty quantification, specifically employing conformal inference techniques, to dynamically adjust inference thresholds in real-time. The system continuously monitors and estimates the uncertainty associated with the network's predictions, and then adjusts the threshold accordingly. This approach aims to provide a more reliable and objective method for inference, reducing the reliance on manual threshold tuning and enhancing the overall performance of Bayesian network applications. The core claim is that determining appropriate thresholds for Bayesian network inference is often subjective and domain-dependent. The core mechanism is the implementation of a system that dynamically adjusts the threshold for inference based on a continuous, real-time quantification of the uncertainty in the network's predictions.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Adversarial Robustness in Deep Learning
abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success in various domains, but their vulnerability to adversarial attacks poses a significant challenge. These attacks, which involve subtle perturbations to input data, can cause models to make incorrect predictions with high confidence. Traditional adversarial training methods, while effective to some extent, often rely on simplifying assumptions about the nature of adversarial perturbations – typically assuming they are drawn from a specific distribution. This paper proposes a novel approach leveraging probabilistic programming languages to address this limitation. We argue that modeling the uncertainty surrounding adversarial perturbations is crucial for building truly robust deep learning systems. Our framework allows us to explicitly represent and reason about the probabilistic nature of these attacks, leading to the design of architectures that are inherently more resilient. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and conceptual design how probabilistic programming can improve adversarial robustness by incorporating variance and distributional information into the learning process. The core of our approach involves defining probabilistic models for adversarial noise, allowing us to condition the deep learning model's output on this uncertainty. This shifts the paradigm from simply minimizing misclassification rates to optimizing for robustness against a range of possible adversarial scenarios.

title: Quantum Routing in Quantum Networks Using Time-Encoded Signals
abstract: This paper proposes a novel routing protocol for quantum networks leveraging the principles of time-encoded quantum signals. The core idea is to utilize the inherent temporal correlations within quantum networks to enable efficient routing and forwarding of quantum information. This approach addresses the significant challenge of routing in quantum networks, where traditional routing protocols based on classical control signals are inapplicable due to the no-cloning theorem and the fragility of quantum states. The proposed protocol utilizes precisely timed pulses of quantum information to navigate the network, effectively creating a "temporal address" for each quantum state. We explore the mathematical framework underpinning this protocol, focusing on the key concepts of quantum state tomography, time-bin encoding, and the resulting network topology. The theoretical analysis demonstrates the potential for high-throughput quantum routing, offering a pathway to improve the overall performance and scalability of quantum networks. The protocol's efficiency hinges on precise timing synchronization and robust error correction strategies, which we briefly discuss.

title: A Program Synthesis Engine Based on Cellular Automata
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis, termed a Cellular Automata-based Program Synthesis Engine. The core idea is to leverage the self-organizing behavior observed in biological cells to automatically generate programs with desired functionalities. This is achieved by translating a given program design problem into a set of rules governing a cellular automaton. The interaction and evolution of these cells then drive the emergence of program code. Furthermore, a genetic algorithm is employed to optimize the quality of the generated code. We demonstrate the feasibility of this methodology through a theoretical framework, outlining the key components and the proposed workflow. The engine's ability to mimic biological processes offers a fundamentally different perspective on program synthesis, potentially leading to more robust and adaptable code generation systems. The primary contribution lies in establishing a concrete, algorithmic approach to program synthesis inspired by cellular automata and evolutionary principles.

title: Quantum Annealing-Based Combinatorial Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum annealing for solving complex combinatorial optimization problems. The core claim is that quantum annealing leverages its global search capabilities to efficiently address such problems. The proposed mechanism involves formulating the combinatorial optimization problem as a quantum annealing problem and utilizing the simulated annealing process within quantum annealing to conduct a search for the optimal solution. This research explores the potential of quantum annealing in practical applications, acknowledging that its application in combinatorial optimization is still in its exploratory phase. The algorithm is designed to minimize the energy of a system described by a Hamiltonian, which evolves over time according to the time-dependent Schrödinger equation. The core of the algorithm lies in mapping the problem's constraints and objective function into this Hamiltonian. The search process is governed by quantum fluctuations, represented by the operator $\hat{H}$, which encourages transitions to lower energy states, effectively navigating the solution space. The effectiveness of the algorithm is evaluated based on the quality of the solution found and the computational resources required. This work provides a foundational exploration of quantum annealing's potential within the field of combinatorial optimization.

title: ##基于记忆增强的深度学习模型
abstract: This paper explores the potential of incorporating memory augmentation techniques into deep learning models to enhance their generalization capabilities and robustness. The core idea is to mimic the human cognitive process of strengthening memories, thereby improving the model's ability to handle unseen data and adversarial attacks. We propose a novel deep learning architecture, termed the Memory-Augmented Deep Neural Network (MADNN), which integrates a memory module to store and retrieve relevant information. The MADNN utilizes a gating mechanism to selectively update its memory based on the input data, effectively creating a learned representation of past experiences. Experimental results demonstrate that the MADNN significantly outperforms traditional deep learning models in tasks requiring long-term dependencies and adaptability to changing environments. The key contribution lies in the practical application of memory augmentation to deep learning, offering a promising approach for building more intelligent and resilient models. We analyze the model's performance across various datasets and demonstrate its superior performance in terms of accuracy, robustness, and generalization.

title: Multi-Scale Spatiotemporal Graphing of Cognitive Architectures
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cognitive architecture based on multi-scale spatiotemporal graphings. The core claim is that cognitive processes can be effectively modeled as such graphings, where each scale represents a distinct cognitive level and temporal dimension, and their dynamic interactions form the basis of cognition. The mechanism relies on integrating information theory and graph theory to construct these graphings and utilizes dynamic network theory to analyze information flow and decision-making processes within them. This approach offers a deeper understanding of cognition by explicitly representing its multi-faceted and evolving nature. Specifically, the architecture is defined by nodes (representing cognitive elements) and edges (representing relationships and flows of information) within the graph. The scales are defined by the granularity of the nodes and the temporal resolution of the edges. The model aims to capture the hierarchical and dynamic organization of cognitive processes, allowing for the simulation and analysis of complex cognitive behaviors. The key contribution lies in providing a framework for quantifying and understanding the interplay between different cognitive levels and their temporal evolution. This framework allows for the formalization of cognitive processes through mathematical representations, enabling computational modeling and theoretical advancements. The presented model incorporates concepts from graph theory, network analysis, and information theory to provide a comprehensive approach to cognitive architecture design.

title: Dynamic Semantic Symbiotic Network (DSN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Semantic Symbiotic Network (DSN), a novel approach to semantic representation and reasoning that leverages the principles of biological neural networks. The core claim of DSN is to achieve real-time, dynamic semantic symbiosis and evolution within complex systems by utilizing distributed, self-organizing neuromorphic hardware nodes. Unlike traditional computational models that rely on static semantic representations, DSN dynamically adapts its semantic landscape through a mechanism of synaptic plasticity and emergent communication within a network of heterogeneous nodes. The system employs "semantic agents" that learn and adapt through feedback, continuously adjusting connection weights to form dynamic semantic graphs based on interactions and external input. This paper details the architecture, core mechanism, and the fundamental innovation of DSN, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of existing semantic networks in handling complex, dynamic, and contextualized semantic information. The system's adaptive nature and biological inspiration offer improved robustness and scalability.

title: Quantum Information Entropy Encoding (QIE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel information encoding scheme, termed Quantum Information Entropy Encoding (QIE), leveraging quantum entanglement and coherence to potentially surpass the entropy limits established by classical information theory. QIE utilizes multi-qubit entanglement states, precisely manipulating their coherence, to establish highly correlated information representations between quantum bits. The encoding process employs quantum gate operations to transform these entangled states, facilitating information compression and transmission. Decoding relies on measurements of the entangled states to recover the original information. The core claim is the potential for QIE to achieve higher compression rates and faster transmission speeds compared to conventional entropy coding methods. This approach represents a departure from traditional information theory, exploring the utilization of quantum mechanical phenomena for enhanced information processing. The theoretical framework presented here lays the groundwork for future investigations into the feasibility and limitations of QIE.

title: Quantum Error Correction Protocol Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates adaptive optimization strategies for quantum error correction (QEC) protocols. The core claim is that dynamically adjusting QEC parameters based on real-time noise assessments can significantly improve correction efficiency. This is achieved through a mechanism utilizing quantum degradation models to monitor noise levels during the error correction process. Subsequently, machine learning algorithms are employed to autonomously optimize QEC parameters, such as encoding rate and redundancy, responding to the dynamic noise environment. The novelty lies in moving beyond fixed-parameter QEC schemes, enhancing robustness and adaptability across varying noise conditions. The proposed approach offers a pathway towards more efficient and reliable quantum information processing. ---
